name: Dispatches
description: An in-depth look at news stories. Documentaries that take you behind the scenes giving an insight into people's lives or institutions.

videos.title: The Plutonium Black Market
videos.overview: Investigating the black market in weapons grade uranium operated from Khartoum.

videos.title: In The Red
videos.overview: Investigation of the alleged misuse of funds at three Labour Party Social Clubs in Dundee.

videos.title: AIDS - The Unheard Voices
videos.overview: The program challenges the theory that AIDS is caused by the H.I.V. virus and discusses the social pressures on those diagnosed as H.I.V. positive.

videos.title: Divided by Law
videos.overview: Explains how new D.N.A. testing techniques could help to re-unite divided immigrant families and looks at claims that the government has delayed progress pending on legislation.

videos.title: Selling the Tunnel
videos.overview: TVS's Business Unit tells the inside story of the Eurotunnel Management Team's battle to persuade the City and the public to back the issue of shares and raise capital.

videos.title: Gunning for Government
videos.overview: The undercover world of arms dealing is revealed by a defector (Frank Turner) who reveals his involvement with the CIA and British Ministry of Defence.

videos.title: Kimberly Carlile - Falling Through the Net
videos.overview: 4 1/2 year old Kimberley was starved, dehydrated and beaten and weighed 24Ibs-small for a normal child her age. Her stepfather Nigel Hall was jailed for life for her murder, the mother Pauline Carlile was jailed 12 years for cruelty.

videos.title: Korea: Poverty Prohibited
videos.overview: In the run-up to the Olympics, the Seoul urban poor are forced from their homes to make way for the developers.

videos.title: The Miner's Debate
videos.overview: A question of concern, doubt and safety of mine workers from around Britain.

videos.title: Waiting for the Consultant
videos.overview: Documentary report which looks at the suitability of doctors' work practices to the needs of the modern National Health Service.

videos.title: Danger! Men at Work
videos.overview: An investigation over sexual harassment at work, the women behind it and what had been done to justify as a court offense.

videos.title: Interview with John Stalker
videos.overview: Interview with John Stalker who recently resigned as Deputy Chief Constable of Manchester. He was removed from an investigation of police and army tactics in Northern Ireland, and has now written a book about his experiences.

videos.title: Iran: A Widening Gulf
videos.overview: Tim Hodlin reports on Iran and it's current state.

videos.title: Palau: Paradise Lost
videos.overview: Documentary report on US policies in the Pacific island of Palau and the seeking of an agreement with the islanders, despite their non-nuclear constitution, to bring nuclear weapons to the island.

videos.title: Working for Welfare
videos.overview: Report on the US system of making the unemployed work for their benefits, called Workfare

videos.title: Radioactive Britain
videos.overview: A report on the Radioactive Substances Act, which permits over 7000 premises throughout Britain to handle radioactive material.

videos.title: The Lobby
videos.overview: Investigation in to the influence of the American Israel Public Affairs Committee (AIPAC), known as "The Lobby", in the United States.

videos.title: Charity Fraud
videos.overview: Report into a number of case histories of alleged charity fraud, which leads to an examination of the loopholes in existing charity laws.

videos.title: Single Union Deals With Employers
videos.overview: Documentary about how the big unions present themselves to potential new employers in contests to sign single-union deals.

videos.title: Cuba From Inside
videos.overview: A report on human rights in Cuba

videos.title: Talking to the Terrorists
videos.overview: Documentary report in which former members of the West German terrorist group, the Red Army Faction, talk about their pasts and their hopes for an amnesty which will let them back into society.

videos.title: Cancer Research
videos.overview: A look at cancer research, and the lack of evidence that there has been much progress over the last 50-60 years. Some researchers think that there is no cure in sight. Why is so little research done into cancer prevention?

videos.title: Freemasonry
videos.overview: The Freemasons have invited cameras into the Grand Lodge at Covent Garden for the first time.

videos.title: War in the Desert
videos.overview: The first documentary about a war that has been going on for 13 years in the Sahara Desert between Morocco and a rebel army known as the Polisario.

videos.title: NATO's Nuclear Programme
videos.overview: Documentary investigation into the nuclear capacity of NATO.

videos.title: Illegal Betting
videos.overview: Documentary report about illegal gambling, worth £400-600 million annually. Hidden cameras are used in pubs and clubs from London to Liverpool.

videos.title: What's Best for the Children? : Coventry
videos.overview: Documentary about a model system in Coventry which has been set up to deal with child abuse, and which it is hoped will avoid most of the problems that occurred in Cleveland.

videos.title: The Raid on San Fernando: Communist Rebels in The Philippines
videos.overview: Documentary made by Nick Downie about the time he spent with the Philippine Communist guerrillas, the New People's Army.

videos.title: The Hashish Connection
videos.overview: Documentary filmed in the Bekaa valley about Lebanon's powerful drug clans.

videos.title: Disciples of Chaos
videos.overview: Documentary report about the National Front, which will be 21 years old this year. They now work mostly underground as a subversive organization. Also reports on Roberto Fiore in Italy.

videos.title: Trouble on the Waterfront
videos.overview: Port employers and the government want to scrap the Dock Labour Scheme, but there is great opposition amongst dockers.

videos.title: The Two State Solution
videos.overview: Documentary report on the attitudes of Israelis and Palestinians to the future of the occupied territories. A look at the idea of forming two separate states, however, people on both sides are opposed to this.

videos.title: Turkey: Trading with Torture
videos.overview: Documentary report on the continued use of torture in Turkey, despite its desire to join the EEC, which bans such practices. Includes graphic personal accounts.

videos.title: Exporting High Technology from West to East
videos.overview: Documentary report about the measures taken by the United States to ensure that their high technology is not exported to the Soviet bloc.

videos.title: Tibet - A Case to Answer
videos.overview: Documentary examining the destruction of the landscape, and the rights and religion of the people of Tibet, which has been ruled by the Chinese for 40 years.

videos.title: The Day the Dream Died
videos.overview: 25 years after the assassination of US President John F. Kennedy, British Channel Four's Dispatches asks the following still unanswered questions: 1) Our evidence points to an inescapable conclusion - this casket is empty. The question is, why? 2) Lyndon B. Johnson - what did this man stand to gain from the death of President Kennedy? 3) Who was this man [at the scene]? 4) Why did all these witnesses have to die? 5) Why was Lee Harvey Oswald arrested so quickly? 6) Who set Jack Ruby up to kill Oswald? 7) Why was it necessary to alter Kennedy's body before the official autopsy in Washington? 8) Why did the Dallas doctors change their testimony the very next day? 9) Why was Kennedy's brain missing at the autopsy in Washington? 10) Why did the Warren commission deceive the world?

videos.title: The Winds of Death
videos.overview: Documentary report on the Iraqi army's poison gas attacks on Kurdish villagers

videos.title: The Battle for Stone Bassett
videos.overview: Documentary investigation into the controversy surrounding the plan to build a new 6000 houses town, Stone Bassett, in rural Oxfordshire.

videos.title: The Countertraders
videos.overview: Documentary examination of the growth of "Countertrade" deals - compensatory agreements made between a government and a foreign company to offset the effects of placing an order overseas.

videos.title: A Very Polish Secret
videos.overview: Documentary about the previously untold story of a 1945 massacre of Polish partisans by Russian troupes and pro-Russian Polish security forces.

videos.title: Return to Year Zero?
videos.overview: Documentary report on the risks to the area if the Khmer Rouge regains power in Kampuchea.

videos.title: Gorbachev's Asylums
videos.overview: Documentary report about the changes in the Soviet Union's psychiatric system caused by Gorbachev's policy of "glasnost".

videos.title: Cooking the Books
videos.overview: Investigation of Thatcher government's alleged misuse of official statistics.

videos.title: The Spy Who Broke the Code
videos.overview: Documentary examining the continued significance for the USA and her allies, of John Walker, a US Navy Chief Warrant Officer and Soviet Spy.

videos.title: Buckets of Money
videos.overview: Documentary investigation into high pressure shares salesmen. Exposes the 'bucket shops' where share dealers are cheating the small investor.

videos.title: The Copper Seven Story
videos.overview: Documentary report abut the legal wrangle in Los Angeles involving G.D. Searle, manufacturers of a contraceptive coil which it was forced to withdraw from the American market.

videos.title: Afghan
videos.overview: A four month Afghan report from the eyes and mouth of Jeff Harmon and Alexander Lindsay.

videos.title: The Toxic Trail
videos.overview: Documentary on the legal debate surrounding a mother's wish to have sterilized her 35-year old daughter, who has a mental age of four.

videos.title: The Return of the Death Squads
Chico
videos.overview: A documentary about the Brazilian Chico Mendes, filmed over several years by Adrian Cowell, about the Brazilian campaigner against deforestation of the Amazon rainforest.

videos.title: The Most Neglected Crime
videos.overview: Four out of ten women had received an unwanted obscene phone call, but a police superintendent could not recall one individual being prosecuted for that offence in 23 years.

videos.title: Not What the Doctor Ordered
videos.overview: Featuring David Willetts of the Centre for Policy Studies, and a new White Paper on health

videos.title: Hungarians Not Comrades
videos.overview: Documentary profile of the people of Hungary, whose country has been the centre of world attention in 1989 with the return of democratic elections.

videos.title: Twelve Days in November
videos.overview: Documentary report from Czechoslovakia on the recent political upheavals over the twelve days since Friday 17th November.

videos.title: Apartheid's Assassins
videos.overview: Over the years many political activists have been murdered in strange circumstances, but security denied that special 'hit squad' units were responsible. Then Captain Dirk Coetzee, ex-commander of one of these units, fled the country and told his story to the ANC, in extensive interviews Coetzee explains the functioning of the special units. The video also reconstructs attacks carried out against Zimbabwean anti-apartheid campaigners.

videos.title: The Arthur Legend
videos.overview: Director Ken Loach and reporter-producer Lorraine Heggessey defend miners' leader Arthur Scargill against allegations made by the Daily Mirror and ITV's The Cook Report (1987-98), including financial misconduct during the 1984-85 miners' strike.

videos.title: The Truth that Sets Us Free
Beyond Faith
videos.overview: Special investigation into Satanic ritual abuse.

videos.title: The Law Of The Ghetto
videos.overview: An investigation into tactics used by the IRA to intimidate citizens of Northern Ireland.

videos.title: Election 1992: The Issue They Don't Debate
The People Of The Shining Path
Pocket Neutron
videos.overview: Following last year's The Trail of Red Mercury (1993), Dispatches now presents new evidence of how Russian scientists have designed a new miniature neutron bomb using red mercury.

videos.title: Shackled Children
videos.overview: Follows the work of activists against child labour in the US, Russia, India, Egypt and Colombia.

videos.title: Accident Waiting to Happen
videos.overview: An investigation into safety standards at football grounds and how they are being ignored in spite of the Taylor and Popplewell reports which were issued after the Hillsborough disaster and Bradford stadium fire. Our reporter uncovers through secret filming the many ways in which football clubs are still ignoring these safety regulations. Club chairman are confronted on camera with the evidence collected and are asked to justify their lack of concern.

videos.title: Insult to Injury
videos.overview: With the increase of insurance claims, insurance companies are involved in a string of scams. This investigation reveals the desperate measures undertaken by insurers to cut their pay out bills. It shows the real-life scam brought on three innocent victims by the use of deceitful tricks and private eyes. The investigation provides 3 people caught in the insurers scams and attempts of interviewing the insurance companies.

videos.title: New Labour, Old Habits?
videos.overview: An investigation into the alleged disreputable behaviour and secretly-recorded comments of Leicester East MP Keith Vaz suggests that Tony Blair's New Labour may not be such a new way of doing politics after all.

videos.title: Estate of Terror
videos.overview: Every year up to two hundred and forty thousand old people suffer form crimes committed by children. Overwhelmingly these crimes take the form of harassment. The elderly are verbally abused, stoned in the street and have their windows smashed. Sometimes the harassment escalates into burglary or even murder. At least 12 old people have been killed by juveniles in the last 4 years. Dispatches contacted all of the main national agencies who care for the elderly and without exception they were all unaware of the extent of the problem. Old people all over Britain are suffering in silence afraid to leave their houses whilst children control the streets.

videos.title: A Bosnian Betrayal
videos.overview: The program explores the extent to which United Nations officials and commanders in Bosnia put the safety of their troops ahead of their responsibility to the civilians in Srebrenica. Although Srebrenica was designated as a United Nations safe haven, the Serbian forces apparently massacred Bosnian Muslims after they captured the city in July, 1995.

videos.title: Trooping Out the Colour
videos.overview: Racism in the British Army.

videos.title: The Search for Mother Russia's Children
The Force is Not with You
Judgement for Louise
videos.overview: Journalist David Jessel and producer Steve Haywood from the acclaimed Trial and Error (1992) come to Dispatches to examine doubts about the safety of the conviction of nanny Louise Woodward for the death of a baby in her care.

videos.title: Golf Lima Foxtrot
videos.overview: GLF is police jargon for "Go Like F***". But does such light-hearted jocularity betray a lack of serious regard for the potential dangers to the public of cops' ability to break the rules of the road when performing high-speed pursuits?

videos.title: The war Business
videos.overview: Journalists uncover the bloody truth of the world's most successful private army, Executive Outcomes. Sent wherever mineral resources like diamonds or oil promise wealth, these mercenaries, trained as soldiers in apartheid-era South Africa and equipped with state-of-the-art weapons of war, sell their security services to the highest bidder and frequently leave a trail of destruction in their wake. And British interests are behind it all.

videos.title: The Accident
videos.overview: Documentary investigating the death of Diana Princess of Wales and Dodi Fayed.

videos.title: The Crime Game
videos.overview: The revelation that police and criminals are playing a mutually beneficial game, in which the latter admit to crimes they have not committed so the former can then show falsely improved crime figures.

videos.title: A Matter of Life and Death
For the Love of a Stranger
Dying for the President
videos.overview: Investigation of alleged war crimes in Chechnya on the eve of Russian elections.

videos.title: The Real Story of the Leeds Fans
The Runaway Cars
videos.overview: In Britain and America, there have been many incidents of Ford cars suddenly accelerating, causing serious injuries and even deaths. However, Ford deny all responsibility, and say that the accidents are caused by driver error.

videos.title: How to Jump the Health Queue
Bloody Foreigners
videos.overview: 'Bloody Foreigners' is Andrew Smith's investigation into the British attitude towards asylum seekers and immigrants who live and work in the UK. It exposes the culture of hypocrisy under which xenophobia proliferates to such an extreme that asylum seekers are physically and verbally abused on a daily basis. It underlines the fact that these very people are working illegally for well under minimum wage, to line the pockets of seemingly legitimate British businesses. Part one reveals the scam behind a government-funded housing project in Liverpool. The owner receives millions from the council for ostensibly offering accommodation to asylum seekers. Yet the blocks of flats are in a shocking state of disrepair, conditions are freezing - not to mention the treatment the occupants receive from the locals. Secret camera footage shows the assault and harassment of inhabitants, regularly inflicted by neighbouring youths.

videos.title: Bloody Foreigners: Part 2
videos.overview: Part two deals with illegal workers who are employed by apparently respectable companies as waitresses, cleaners, and builders, to name but a few, without any legal documents or insurance, and paid as little a £20 for a long day. The final section uses hidden cameras to show the trade in forged passports which is rife in Finsbury Park Mosque, north London.

videos.title: Unforgiven: The Boys Who Murdered James Bulger
videos.overview: The documentary covers the outcry from the population after hearing about the release of the two boys who killed 2 year-old James Bulger in 1993. Presenting the protests against their release from an institution, the film also gives a background about the killers, their terrible violent act and the impact it caused in UK.

videos.title: Beneath the Veil
videos.overview: British journalist Saira Shah travels to Afghanistan with a camera crew to document the realities of life under the Taliban. Filmed just months prior to the terrorist attacks of September 11, 2001, the footage reveals the chilling brutality of a fledgling government made up of radicalized followers of Osama bin Laden.

videos.title: Outbreak: The True Story of Foot and Mouth
videos.overview: A critical look at the handling of the Foot-and-mouth outbreak from February 2001 until June 2001.

videos.title: Unholy War
videos.overview: Reporter Saira Shah returns to Afghanistan in the aftermath of the September 11th terrorists attacks. She reunites with three Afghan girls who were forced to watch as her mother was executed by Taliban soldiers. She also tours Northern Alliance fortifications and profiles an aid worker from the United States.

videos.title: Young, Nazi and Proud
videos.overview: Dispatches reporter David Modell films a remarkable six months spent in the questionable company of Mark Collett, leader of the youth wing of the British National Party, and reveals the true nature of a party trying to reinvent itself and broaden its appeal.

videos.title: Lifting the Veil
videos.overview: One year on from when she secretly entered Afghanistan to film her original tv special "Beneath the Veil" (2001) (TV) Saira Shah re-visits and investigates the story of a woman whose public execution had been secretly filmed in the first film and to see if women's situation had improved after the fall of the Taliban

videos.title: The Killing Zone
videos.overview: Dispatches revisits the Gaza Strip to focus on civilians caught in the crossfire of never-ending battles. We meet seriously injured children and their distraught families, and the International Solidarity Movement whose member Tom Hurndall is shot. Then it hits even closer to home, when previous Dispatches director and cameraman James Miller is shot dead while he and Saira Shah are making another of their films together.

videos.title: Blood and Revenge
videos.overview: Channel 4's Dispatches reporter Sam Kiley reveals the inside story of the Iraqi Kurds' homecoming, travelling with their fighters, the Peshmerga, as they re-take Kirkuk from forces loyal to Saddam.

videos.title: Virgin Soldiers
videos.overview: With unprecedented access, award winning filmmaker Dodge Billingsley tells the story of India Company 3rd Battalion, 7th Marine regiment, crack U.S. frontline troops in Iraq. With some as young as 19, the invasion of Iraq was the first time any of them had actually been sent into combat. Experience a day in the life of these young men as they play a vital role in the liberation of Iraq. With remarkable battle footage, Virgin Soldiers reveals the true story of men who fought their way into the heart of Baghdad.

videos.title: What Hutton Won't Tell You
videos.overview: As the Hutton report is published, the actions of the government once again come under minute scrutiny.

videos.title: Third Class Post
videos.overview: In a special investigation, Dispatches reporter Simon Barnes goes undercover inside the Royal Mail to reveal a damning catalogue of skiving workers, ineffective managers and gangs of criminals stealing millions of pounds from the post.

videos.title: Keep Them Out
videos.overview: Award-winning Dispatches director David Modell, investigates how public opinion is affecting the Government's policy on asylum by travelling to Lee-on-the-Solent and revealing how this small town in the south of England reacts when threatened with an influx of asylum seekers.

videos.title: Fit to Eat
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates whether out-sourcing hospital meals to cook-chill cook-freeze food suppliers means that patients are not always receiving all the nutrients that they need for recovery and investigates whether appropriate standards of hygiene are being met.

videos.title: MMR: What They Didn't Tell You
Dispatches Live Special: After the Tsunami
The NHS - Your Money or Your Life?
Beslan
videos.overview: The school siege at Beslan on September 1st, 2004 left 334 dead and a small town in shock, having to come to terms with the loss of so many of its people.

videos.title: The Big Heist
videos.overview: Just before Christmas 2004, two men dressed as police officers arrive at a remote home and, after tricking their way inside the house they take the family hostage. Meanwhile at another house a second family is taken hostage. The reason for both movements was to gain control over two key employees of the Northern Bank in Belfast. The next day, while the families are still held, the employees are used to carry over £26,000,000 in cash out of the bank in broad daylight. This documentary looks at who did the robbery and how the failings of the British government contributed to the freedom of the robbers to act.

videos.title: What's Really in Your Christmas Dinner
Ryanair: Caught Napping
videos.overview: A behind-the-scenes look at low budget airline Ryanair. Uncovering security and health and safety breaches, uncleaned aircraft and long staff working hours.

videos.title: After School Arms Club
videos.overview: Two groups of high school kids, one from England and one from Ireland set up shop as online arms dealers and broker various deals, shipping arms from the far east to homes in America.

videos.title: How to Beat Your Kid's Asthma: Part 1
How to Beat Your Kid's Asthma: Part 2
Iraq: The Women's Story
videos.overview: An anonymous woman who is not a journalist blends in with the women of Iraq to find out what life is really like for them.

videos.title: Mad About Animals
videos.overview: Following Animal Liberation activists.

videos.title: The Labour Loans Scandal
videos.overview: An investigation into the secret world of the funding of the Labour Party.

videos.title: The Drug Trial That Went Wrong
The Dispatches Debate: Muslims and Free Speech
Jihad TV
videos.overview: Videos of suicide bombers and insurgent attacks have become an important weapon for Al Qaeda. But who watches these videos and what effect are they having on young people in the Muslim world?

videos.title: NHS Postcode Lottery
videos.overview: How does the care you receive at your local hospital compare with the rest of the UK? Jon Snow reveals the true scale of the NHS postcode lottery, which is denying some patients vital drugs while others receive the same treatment elsewhere

videos.title: Undercover Mosque
videos.overview: Investigative journalist, Bobby Pathak, has investigated a number of mosques run by high profile national organisations that claim to be dedicated to moderation and dialogue with other faiths. But reporting undercover he joined worshippers to find a message of religious bigotry and extremism being preached. The investigation reveals Saudi Arabian universities are recruiting young Western Muslims to train them in their extreme theology, then sending them back to the West to spread the word.

videos.title: At Home with the Terror Suspects
NHS: Where Did All the Money Go?
Greenwash
videos.overview: The government is set to achieve only a third to a half of its overall policy target for reducing greenhouse gas emissions by 2020. Dispatches reports. The expert-reviewed audit by the UCL Environment Institute is the first comprehensive investigation into the real impact of the Government's carbon-cutting policies across all government departments mandated with reducing greenhouse gas emissions

videos.title: When Did You Last Beat Your Wife?
Between the Mullahs and The Military
Drinking Yourself to Death
videos.overview: Based on medical research and personal findings Dispatches investigates the effects binge drinking can have on a consumer's health and whether low-priced (supermarket bought) alcohol is one of the causes for an increase in alcohol consumption.

videos.title: Undercover Mother
videos.overview: Tazeen Ahmad investigates the overstretched maternity services which are resulting in new mothers having traumatic births and at worst, putting lives at risk.

videos.title: Nice Work If You Can Get It
videos.overview: Political journalist Peter Oborne examines how politicians and MPs use their power to gain financial benefits.

videos.title: Immigrants: The Inconvenient Truth
videos.overview: Looks at the beneficial social and economical contributions made by different immigrant groups, drawing on research done by the Institute for Public Policy Research. Contrasts this with the perception of immigrants and political and media issues.

videos.title: China's Stolen Children
videos.overview: Ten years after the policy-changing and award-winning film, The Dying Rooms, the same team returns to a very different China where the infamous One Child Policy has had the horrific side effect of a boom in stolen children. With extraordinary access to devastated parents desperately searching for their stolen son; a man who brokers the deals and has sold his own offspring; and prospective parents grappling with giving up their soon-to-be-born daughter through lack of options, we are brought face to face with the crisis that such a stringent government policy has created among China's poorest people

videos.title: Abortion: What We Need to Know
videos.overview: An investigation into abortion; focusing on how new scientific research on foetal pain could cause for a change to current abortion laws.

videos.title: Searching for Madeleine
videos.overview: After the disappearance of child, Madeline McCann 168 days ago; Dispatches sent a team of five of the UK's best-qualified criminal investigators to Praia da Luz to investigate and assess the situation.

videos.title: How to Get Ahead in Africa
Mark Thomas on Coca-Cola
videos.overview: Comedian and activist Mark Thomas reports on how Coca-Cola has caused problems in the world with pollution, worker exploitation and even death. The documentary also reports on how Coca-Cola respond to these allegations.

videos.title: How Safe Are Your Christmas Toys?
videos.overview: Deborah Davies reports on potentially dangerous toys that can be bought in the UK. These toys are then safety tested and the findings reported to authorities

videos.title: The Truth About Your Food: Part 1
The Truth About Your Food: Part 2
The Court of Ken
videos.overview: With just months to go before Londoners vote for the next Mayor of London, the current affairs series investigates the current mayoral system and takes an in depth look at current Mayor, Ken Livingstone and the how he has misused his power to his advantage.

videos.title: Why Kids Kill
videos.overview: A report on the increase of gang culture and murder that teenagers participate in the UK.

videos.title: Heat or Eat, the Pensioners' Dilemma
How the Banks Bet Your Money
Iraq: The Lost Generation
videos.overview: Filmmaker Sharmeen Obaid-Chinoy investigates the biggest and most catastrophic refugee crisis in the Middle East since the Palestinian diaspora of 1948.

videos.title: Undercover in Tibet
videos.overview: Reveals the regime of terror which dominates daily life and makes freedom of expression an impossibility.

videos.title: In God's Name
videos.overview: An investigation into the growth of Christian fundamentalism in the UK.

videos.title: Gordon Brown: Where Did It All Go Wrong?
The Truth About Food Prices
videos.overview: A report on the rising cost of food prices and the impact it has producers and consumers.

videos.title: A Widow's War on Yobs
videos.overview: This documentary follows widow, Helen Newlove. Her husband Gary was kicked to death outside their home in Cheshire. This film follows her journey to tackle youth crime in the UK.

videos.title: It Shouldn't Happen to a Muslim
videos.overview: On the third anniversary of the 7/7 London bombings Peter Oborne investigates whether the has fueled anger and violence towards British Muslims.

videos.title: The Jab That Can Stop Cancer
videos.overview: A new jab will be offered to every girl aged 12 to 13 in Britain to help protect her against cervical cancer. While some hail it as a medical breakthrough, it has provoked controversy.

videos.title: Sandwiches Unwrapped
videos.overview: An examination of Britain's sandwich industry and whether shop-bought sandwiches are as healthy for you as consumers think.

videos.title: Undercover Mosque: The Return
videos.overview: A year and a half after Undercover Mosque, this follow-up documentary goes undercover again to investigate extremism in the UK.

videos.title: Hope for the Last Chance Kids
videos.overview: Update on the pupils of Monteagle Primary School featured in an earlier documentary. The pupils experience a remarkable improvement as a result of using synthetic phonics.

videos.title: What's in Your Wine?
videos.overview: Jane Moore investigates scandals in the wine industry, taking a look at the 40 different substances that can be used in producing wine but which are rarely detailed on the label of your bottle of wine.

videos.title: The Human Cost of the Credit Crunch
The Hidden World of Lap Dancing
videos.overview: An investigation into lap dancing clubs in England and whether they abide by the rules stated on their entertainment license

videos.title: The Truth about Your Energy Bill
videos.overview: Deborah Davies investigates the rising price of energy bills in the UK. She finds out why our charges are so high, whether changing suppliers can reduce bills, and the impact of Gordon Brown's fuel package.

videos.title: Saving Africa's Witch Children
videos.overview: Reporting on children in parts Nigeria branded as witches.

videos.title: Mum, Dad, Alzheimer's & Me
videos.overview: Journalist Fiona Phillips tells the very personal story of her father's developing Alzheimer's disease, and how it affects him and the family as a whole.

videos.title: The True Cost of Cheap Food
videos.overview: After looking at rising prices in The Truth About Food Prices, Rayner now looks at the other end of the scale - the new cheap food ranges and whether they have a true higher cost ... our health.

videos.title: Unseen Gaza
videos.overview: Jon Snow explores the difficulties faced by news organisations around the world in reporting the conflict in Gaza. Who is getting the true picture of events as they happen?

videos.title: Too Old to Work
videos.overview: With the number of unemployed in the UK nudging two million, Dispatches reveals the ageism rife amongst employers and recruitment agencies.

videos.title: The Big Job Hunt
videos.overview: An investigation into rising unemployment in the UK and what steps the government are taking to alleviate it.

videos.title: Confessions of a Nurse
videos.overview: Following a YouGov report Dispatches takes a candid look at the NHS nursing system - with interviews from nurses and undercover footage.

videos.title: Crash: How the Banks Went Bust!
Crash: How Long Will It Last?
Rape in the City
videos.overview: After two recent, high-profile cases in which young women have been attacked and raped by groups of men; Journalist Sorious Samura investigates gang rape in the UK.

videos.title: Battle Scarred
videos.overview: Follows the stories of four soldiers returning from the combat zones in the middle-east and the impact it has had on their lives and the people around them.

videos.title: Middle Class and Jobless
videos.overview: Examining middle-class unemployment in Britain.

videos.title: Cops on the Cheap?
videos.overview: A look at Police Community Support Officers who patrol the streets and cost the taxpayers millions. This documentary questions if they are good value.

videos.title: Lords, Billionaires and the Russian Connection
My Family and Alzheimer's
videos.overview: Fiona Phillips returns to the issue of Alzheimer's treatment, examining whether there has been any improvement in the provision of financial support and respite care available for them and their carers.

videos.title: The Slumdog Children of Mumbai
videos.overview: This Dispatches Special , screening as part of Channel 4's Indian Winter season, reveals the brutal reality of life on the streets and in the slums of Mumbai, following the daily struggles of four young children to survive.

videos.title: Afghanistan: Behind Enemy Lines
videos.overview: Dispatches goes inside the enemy camp in northern Afghanistan as award-winning Afghan reporter Najibullah Quraishi is granted access to an army of extreme Islamic combatants.

videos.title: Post Office Undercover
videos.overview: Two reporters go undercover as agency postmen to find out if the Royal Mail has delivered on claims that it is modernizing and improving its service.

videos.title: Kids Don't Count
videos.overview: An investigation into the rise of school children who are struggling with mathematics and tries to find solutions.

videos.title: Kids Don't Count: Part 2
videos.overview: In the second half of the two-part special, maths specialist Richard Dunne returns to Barton Hill Primary School, accompanied by Countdown's Rachel Riley, to help the pupils with their mental arithmetic.

videos.title: Britain's Islamic Republic
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates a fundamentalist Islamic group headquartered in Britain, and its claims to have placed its "brothers" in positions of political power here.

videos.title: Cameron Uncovered
videos.overview: According to polls, after 13 years in the political wilderness, the Conservatives under David Cameron's leadership seem likely to form the next government. Andrew Rawnsley brings viewers an inside portrait of the government that might be.

videos.title: Children of Gaza
videos.overview: Jezza Neumann arrived in Gaza to follow the lives of 3 children over a year. Surrounded by the remnants of the demolished Gaza Strip and increasingly isolated by the blockade that prevents anyone from rebuilding their homes and their lives.

videos.title: Politicians for Hire
videos.overview: After the MPs' expenses scandal, dispatches delves into the world of political lobbying.

videos.title: Tracing the Marathon's Millions
videos.overview: An investigation into how the London marathon's charity earnings are spent and the true cost of how much is spent in staging the event.

videos.title: Election Uncovered
videos.overview: It's nearly time to vote and the campaigning is reaching a climax. Journalist Ben Laurance analyses each party's campaign and gets a real taste of what's happening behind the scenes in the run-up to polling day.

videos.title: The Lost Girls of South Africa
videos.overview: South Africa has the highest incidence of rape and 80% of the victims are girls under 13. The trauma of 5 such girls in Port Elizabeth is discussed. Ineffective police, lax judiciary and the stretched social welfare system are highlighted.

videos.title: Undercover Social Worker
videos.overview: Investigating child protection procedures and practices within the child social care institution.

videos.title: How the Banks Won
videos.overview: Next week's emergency budget will bring more cuts and tax rises to help pay for the bank bailout. Will Hutton investigates the banks and what they've done with our money.

videos.title: How to Save £100 Billion - Live
videos.overview: On the eve of the emergency budget announcement, in a live hour-long debate, Dispatches sets out controversial cuts that could save Britain £100 billion.

videos.title: Africa's Last Taboo
videos.overview: An investigation into the persecution that gay people face in Africa.

videos.title: Gun Nation
videos.overview: Following an undercover police operation to tackle gun crime in the UK.

videos.title: Catching the Gun Runners
videos.overview: For the last two years, Dispatches has been following an undercover police operation as it tracks a criminal gang trying to smuggle guns into Britain.

videos.title: Britain's Witch Children
videos.overview: Dispatches looks at why some of Britain's African churches perpetuate the myth of witchcraft and believe children can be possessed by evil spirits.

videos.title: When Cousins Marry
videos.overview: Looking at the consequences of first cousin marriage in Britain.

videos.title: Britain's Secret Slaves
videos.overview: A look at domestic workers who come to the UK from other countries and end up being mistreated by having their human rights violated by their employers.

videos.title: How the MoD wastes our billions
videos.overview: Veteran war correspondent Sam Kiley turns his sights on the critical issue of whether the British tax payer, and British soldier, are getting value for money from the Ministry of Defence.

videos.title: What's the Point of the Unions?
videos.overview: An inside look at the inner workings of trade unions and examining what could happen if Britain undergoes mass industrial action.

videos.title: Tabloids, Tories and Telephone Hacking
videos.overview: An investigation into the News of the World phone hacking scandal and News International's working relationship with the police, politicians and the current government.

videos.title: Bravo's Deadly Mission
videos.overview: Following a team of US marines as they go on Operation Moshtarak.

videos.title: How the Rich Beat the Taxman
videos.overview: An investigation into the clever tactics wealthy British people and companies use to cheat the tax system.

videos.title: Iraq's Secret War Files
videos.overview: Exposing the full and unreported horror of the Iraqi conflict and its aftermath. The programme reveals the scale of civilian casualties, and allegations that after the scandal of Abu Ghraib, soldiers continued to abuse prisoners; and that US forces did not intervene in the torture and murder of detainees by the Iraqi security services.

videos.title: Britain's Street Kids
videos.overview: Exploring hidden world of runaway and evicted teenagers, looking at their lives and how they fend for themselves.

videos.title: Fashion's Dirty Secret
videos.overview: An investigation into factories that manufacture clothing for high street shops.

videos.title: Riding Europe's Gravy Train
videos.overview: Dispatches reveals the exceptionally generous package of salary, pension and expenses that MEPs receive and how some have abused the rules to pocket as much cash as possible.

videos.title: City of Fear
videos.overview: Following the police and people of Islamabad as Pakistan's capital battles to overcome an unprecedented wave of terrorist attacks.

videos.title: The Kids Britain Doesn't Want
videos.overview: Exploring the experiences of young people who have been brutalized by the asylum system in the UK.

videos.title: The Battle for Haiti
videos.overview: On the night of the Haiti earthquake something happened in downtown Port au Prince - which would leave the fate of all the aid efforts and the country's future hanging in the balance: 4,500 prisoners escaped from Haiti's prison.

videos.title: Fish Unwrapped
videos.overview: An investigation into the fish sold on Britain's high street to find out where it is sourced, how it is processed and what is actually in it.

videos.title: Tabloid's Dirty Secrets
videos.overview: Following the resignation of the Downing Street's head of communications Andy Coulson, charting the unfolding events in the phone hacking scandal.

videos.title: Lessons in Hate and Violence
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover to investigate allegations that, behind closed doors, some Muslim secondary schools in Britain run by Islamic organizations teach a message of hatred and intolerance.

videos.title: The Truth About Hospital Food
videos.overview: Reporter Mark Sparrow examines the quality of hospital food after his 10 week stay in hospital. With people leaving hospitals malnourished and complaints of disgusting food, the reporter asks if something can be done.

videos.title: Secret NHS Diaries
videos.overview: Looking at what care is like for three people during the last weeks of their lives, at home, in a care home, and in hospital.

videos.title: Selling Off Britain
videos.overview: A live debate asking whether Britain should sell off its assets to cut the national debt.

videos.title: Britain's Secret Fat Cats
videos.overview: Investigating whether private outsourcing companies are set to benefit from the government's cuts to public sector funding.

videos.title: Train Journeys from Hell
videos.overview: Investigating complaints of overcrowded trains, delays, cancellations and high ticket prices on British railway journeys.

videos.title: BP: In Deep Water
videos.overview: An investigation into oil company BP - reporting on its oil spills in the gulf of Mexico and similar incidents and its relationship with Government.

videos.title: Cashing in on Degrees
videos.overview: A look at the rise in University fees and those who enjoy the perks and privileges from them.

videos.title: Undercover Hospital
videos.overview: An undercover investigation in one of the country's busiest NHS hospitals as it faces multi-million-pound cuts and hundreds of job losses in the next year.

videos.title: A Year Inside Number 10
videos.overview: A look at the coalition government one year on - looking at the trial and tribulations they faced.

videos.title: The Truth About Going Under the Knife
videos.overview: Investigating whether new innovations in medical procedures and technologies can compromise patient safety.

videos.title: The Truth About Your Dentist
videos.overview: Sam Lister, The Times' Health Editor, investigates NHS dentists looking at dentists which overcharge patients for treatments and constraints the NHS causes.

videos.title: America's Secret Killers
videos.overview: An investigation into America's 'kill/capture' programme to discover new evidence of the strategy's impact, and its costs.

videos.title: The Thief Catchers
videos.overview: A look at a radical scheme in Bristol to deal with repeat criminal offender

videos.title: Conservation's Dirty Secrets
videos.overview: Dispatches reporter Oliver Steeds travels the globe to investigate the conservation movement and its major organizations.

videos.title: The Real Price of Gold
videos.overview: A look at the British gold industry focusing on ethical sources, mining techniques and gold recycling.

videos.title: Landlords from Hell
videos.overview: An investigation into rogue landlords offering shoddy housing and the illegal practices they use to exploit tenants.

videos.title: Murder on Honeymoon
videos.overview: A look at the murder of Anni Dewani - a woman who died under mysterious circumstances on her honeymoon in South Africa.

videos.title: How to buy a football club
videos.overview: A look at how easy it is for ex-players and businessmen to bypass football regulations to gain a profit from selling football clubs.

videos.title: Murdoch: The Mogul Who Screwed the News
The Truth About Drugs in Football
videos.overview: Investigates the use of both recreational and performance-enhancing substances in football.

videos.title: Gypsy Eviction: The Fight for Dale Farm
videos.overview: On the day that the mass eviction was due to start on Dale Farm, Britain's largest traveller site, investigates the controversial relations between gypsies and travellers, their neighbours and the law.

videos.title: The Wonderful World of Tony Blair
videos.overview: Peter Oborne investigates the former PM's eight figure fortune that he has accrued since departing Downing Street in June 2007. The bulk of his income is through his consultancy firm, Tony Blair Associates but shrouded in secrecy it is not clear who they are consulting for.

videos.title: Can You Trust Your Doctor?
videos.overview: Revealing the failing doctors that slip through the net.

videos.title: Britain's Rubbish
videos.overview: An investigation into Britain's waste disposal industry, exposing criminals who profit from illegal dumping and looking at what actually happens to the recycling.

videos.title: Britain's Sex Gangs
videos.overview: Investigates street gangs that groom young girls for sex.

videos.title: Landlords from Hell: Update
videos.overview: A follow up to this years earlier programme, investigating rogue landlords and Britain's bad housing

videos.title: Olympic Tickets for Sale
videos.overview: A look at who got tickets for the London 2012 Olympic games and whether private companies are profiting.

videos.title: The Great Ticket Scandal
videos.overview: An investigation into two major 'fan-to-fan' ticket exchange websites to investigate who is selling via their websites and why so many tickets appear at over the face value so soon after the box office sells out.

videos.title: Watching the Detectives
videos.overview: Revealing how easy it is to buy our most personal and confidential information.

videos.title: Beating the Recession - Cash vs Cards
videos.overview: Investigating whether cutting up our credit cards and paying for everything in cash could leave us with more money in our pockets

videos.title: The Real Mr & Mrs Assad
videos.overview: Investigates the extent of the Assad family's culpability and the chains of command that link the President and select inner circle to the brutal crackdown.

videos.title: Murdoch, Cameron and the £8 billion deal
videos.overview: Investigates just how close the Prime Minister got to the Murdoch empire. Did the Tories agree to help the mogul secure a business deal worth £8 billion?

videos.title: Let Our Dad Die
videos.overview: Tony Nicklinson had a catastrophic stroke, which has left him utterly paralyzed. He has what is known as 'locked in syndrome' and cannot move, talk, feed himself or perform even the most basic function without help.

videos.title: Undercover Undertaker
videos.overview: Lifts the lid on the funeral industry.

videos.title: Cashing in on the Games
videos.overview: Reporter Morland Sanders goes in search of the people cashing in on the 2012 London Olympic Games, and questions whether the overall economic benefits of hosting the event have been oversold.

videos.title: Secrets of the Taxman
videos.overview: An investigation into tax avoidance.

videos.title: Myths About Your 5 a Day
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates what's happened to the five-a-day campaign, which was designed to get us all eating more fruit and veg. Reporter Jane Moore reveals how this vital health message has been hijacked as a marketing tactic.

videos.title: Can You Trust Your Bank?
videos.overview: Jon Snow travels around the UK, meeting consumers, businesses and bankers, to ask whether we can trust our banks.

videos.title: Britain on the Sick
videos.overview: Investigates the controversial processes used to assess whether sickness and disability benefit claimants should be declared fit for work.

videos.title: Britain's High Street Gamble
videos.overview: A look at the rise in high street betting shops and the social effect they have.

videos.title: Tricks of the Dole Cheats
videos.overview: Investigates Jobcentre Plus, the organization tasked with getting Britain back to work and cracking down on dole cheats.

videos.title: Property Nightmare: The Truth About Leaseholds
videos.overview: Investigates allegations of private landlords, councils, and housing associations overcharging leasehold homeowners for housing works and maintenance.

videos.title: The School Dinner Scandal
videos.overview: Tazeen Ahmad examines evidence that strategies to improve the food served in all our schools are fast coming undone.

videos.title: Secrets of Poundland
videos.overview: As other High Street retailers struggle for survival, discount leader Poundland is booming. Its pre-tax profits are up an astonishing 50% in a year. Dispatches' Harry Wallop asks how Poundland sells so cheaply, yet makes so much money.

videos.title: Undercover Retirement Home
videos.overview: Investigating the multi-million pound retirement property industry.

videos.title: Cruises Undercover: The Truth Below Deck
videos.overview: Investigate the reality of life below deck for the multi-national workforce who toil behind the scenes of luxurious ocean going holidays.

videos.title: Secrets of Your Boss's Pay
videos.overview: Follows the former Greggs chief executive Sir Michael Darrington as he launches a campaign to call a halt to corporate greed.

videos.title: Do You Know Your Partner's Past?
videos.overview: Tina Nash investigates 'Clare's Law', a new pilot scheme in which men and women are warned by the authorities about their partners' history of violence.

videos.title: Getting Rich on the NHS
videos.overview: Morland Sanders examines whether the rapid handover of services to private contractors is really good for the public purse, and good for patient care.

videos.title: Nuclear War Games
videos.overview: Provides unprecedented insight into Israel's internal tensions concerning an attack between Israel and Iran which, if escalates, could have major implications for global stability.

videos.title: Chinese Murder Mystery
videos.overview: A look at the life and death of Neil Percival Heywood and whether he was actually murdered. His death, virtually unnoticed at the time, has gone on to shake China's Communist Party to the core.

videos.title: MPs: Are They Still at It?
videos.overview: Two years after the MPs expenses scandal, Dispatches examines whether our parliamentarians are still abusing the system. The investigation discovers a system still with problems and a lack of transparency.

videos.title: Where Has Your Aid Money Gone?
videos.overview: Jonathan Miller travels to Rwanda - the jewel in the crown of British overseas aid - to investigate what British taxes have paid for, and to ask what our government has achieved with the influence our aid supposedly buys us.

videos.title: The Chinese Are Coming
videos.overview: As China continues to flex its financial muscle by buying into British airports, water and breakfast cereals, Dispatches investigates growing Chinese power in the UK.

videos.title: How Safe is Your Cash?
videos.overview: Reporter Morland Sanders investigates whether security procedures that our banks tell us are impenetrable really are? He meets customers who say they have lost thousands of pounds through chip and pin fraud.

videos.title: The American School Massacre
videos.overview: Matt Frei reports from the scene of one of America's worst mass shootings, unravelling the chain of events and asking whether this latest tragedy will lead to a real change in America's attitude to guns.

videos.title: Secrets of Your Car Insurance
videos.overview: Investigates claims that major insurers cash in when you have a crash, through maximizing profits, lucrative referral fees and rebate deals, sometimes at the expense of doing what's best for you and your car.

videos.title: Sharing Mum and Dad
videos.overview: Today, 1 in 3 children in the UK grow up in a home with only one parent. Are we doing what's best for the children of separated parents? Dispatches investigates the current situation surrounding shared parenting after divorce or separation

videos.title: Secrets of Your Supermarket Shop
videos.overview: A look at rising food price and the comparison between different supermarket stores, food markets and independent shops.

videos.title: Weight Watchers: How They Make Their Millions
videos.overview: Investigates the UK's largest diet brand: Weight Watchers.

videos.title: Britain's Hidden Child Abuse
videos.overview: In a year-long investigation, other victims of child abuse from this closed community express their anger about the lack of justice caused by their leaders' misguided approach to dealing with the issue.

videos.title: How Safe Is Your Child's Nursery?
videos.overview: As the government unveils its plans to increase the number of children each nursery staff member is allowed to look after, Dispatches investigates whether parents can really trust their child's nursery.

videos.title: The Horse Meat Scandal
videos.overview: From burgers to ready meals, Britain's horse meat scandal has grown and grown. For Dispatches, Morland Sanders asks how Britain's meat supplies became so contaminated with unauthorized horse meat and who is to blame?

videos.title: Britain on Benefits
videos.overview: The Disability Living Allowance helps more than 3 million people lead useful lives. But the benefit bill has to be cut, and the gov't plans to take more than half a million claimants off DLA. What will that mean for those who depend on it?

videos.title: Death on the Wards
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates the truth behind allegations that tens of thousands of seriously ill people have been put on a pathway to death. That doctors have callously killed off patients who could have had months or even years to live.

videos.title: Undercover Designer Dogs
videos.overview: Designer dogs are all the rage with celebrities and many animal lovers. But Dispatches has discovered a darker side to this canine phenomenon: thousands of puppies are being imported illegally into Britain every year from Eastern Europe.

videos.title: Rich and on Benefits
videos.overview: In budget week Michael Buerk investigates claims that Britain's pensioners are part of an untouchable group when it comes to government welfare cuts and that some should not be receiving any help at all.

videos.title: The Truth About Junior Doctors
videos.overview: Three years ago, European regulations were brought in to limit hours and to protect both doctors and patients. In this Dispatches, Dr Christian discovers that junior doctors across Britain are still regularly working up to 100 hours a week

videos.title: Immigration Undercover
videos.overview: In this report Morland Sanders investigates whether Britain's immigration system is fit for purpose with reports that tens of thousands of files sit uncleared in the system and a large backlog of immigration cases not dealt with.

videos.title: Syria: Across the Lines
videos.overview: A remarkable film from award-winning documentary maker Olly Lambert who has spent weeks living deep inside Syrian territory - with both gov't and opposition supporters - to explore how the 2 year old conflict is tearing communities apart.

videos.title: Britain's Millionaire Criminals
videos.overview: Why are some convicted criminals still enjoying luxury lifestyles funded by their ill-gotten gains? Dozens of fraudsters, drug dealers and money launderers are still enjoying the high life despite being convicted of serious crimes.

videos.title: Secrets of Your Missing Mail
videos.overview: With shoppers increasingly relying on private parcel companies to deliver online purchases, Dispatches goes undercover to find out why couriers sometimes fail to deliver.

videos.title: Murdered in Tenerife
videos.overview: In 2011, Jennifer Mills-Westley, a 60-year-old British grandmother, was attacked and publicly beheaded in broad daylight in Tenerife. Traumatized by the event, her family have never spoken in detail - until tonight.

videos.title: The Hunt for Britain's Sex Gangs
videos.overview: Three years ago Telford police allowed cameras to start filming what became one of the biggest child sex abuse cases in the UK. The investigation, Operation Chalice, encompassed over 100 victims, and around 200 suspected perpetrators

videos.title: Boston, Woolwich & the New Terror
videos.overview: On 15 April two bombs exploded at the finishing line of the Boston Marathon. Just over a month later a British soldier was run over and hacked to death on a London street. The images from either side of the Atlantic shocked the world.

videos.title: Diets, Drugs and Diabetes
videos.overview: Dr. Deborah Cohen, investigations editor at the British Medical Journal, examines a new generation of diabetes drugs that some drug companies hope could also be a magic treatment for obesity.

videos.title: How Councils Waste Your Money
videos.overview: Councils across the UK have annual budgets in the tens of billions of pounds. But do you know what they really spend it on?

videos.title: The Police's Dirty Secret
videos.overview: Dispatches exposes the shocking story of Britain's secret police and how undercover officers reportedly used sex and lies to spy on members of the public. Dispatches reveals the names of high-profile targets spied on by the police.

videos.title: The Prince and His Secret Properties
videos.overview: Last year Prince Charles earned more than £18 million from the Duchy of Cornwall, but how much do we know about this secretive estate? A hugely profitable property empire and the amount of tax Prince Charles is paying.

videos.title: South Africa's Dirty Cops
videos.overview: With South Africa's future under the spotlight, Channel 4 Dispatches examines allegations that the country's police have become a brutal and corrupt force.

videos.title: Taliban Child Fighters
videos.overview: More than 200 children convicted of fighting for the Taliban are currently being held in special prisons across Afghanistan. Their crimes include the laying of improvised explosive devices, ambush and the preparation of suicide missions.

videos.title: NHS Undercover
videos.overview: Two undercover reporters reveal worrying failings in the new NHS 111 call system. Working as trainee call handlers, the reporters filmed evidence of patients left waiting, concerns about training, and staff shortages.

videos.title: Celebs, Brands and Fake Fans
videos.overview: Dispatches investigate what's real and what's fake in the brave new world of Facebook, YouTube and Twitter, exposing new tricks used by marketers to plug brands, from buying fake Facebook 'likes' to influencing social media conversations.

videos.title: Ryanair: Secrets from the Cockpit
videos.overview: Channel 4's flagship current affairs programme: Dispatches, hears from pilots of Europe's biggest airline about their concerns around passenger safety.

videos.title: The Paedophile MP: How Cyril Smith Got Away with It
Secrets of Your Pay Packet
videos.overview: Morland Sanders meets employees at some of Britain's biggest businesses who say they're paying for the bosses' cost-cutting measures and, while profits have gone up, their working conditions may never recover.

videos.title: The Property Market Undercover
videos.overview: Reporter Antony Barnett secretly films the latest tactics used by estate agents to secure sales and commissions and asks whether some agents are even willing to lie to seal the deal.

videos.title: Energy Bills Exposed
videos.overview: Energy bills are on the rise and in the news. Consumers are furious. The Labour Party wants a price freeze. John Major wants a windfall tax. But the big six energy firms say it's not their fault prices are so high.

videos.title: Can You Trust Your Surgeon?
videos.overview: Dispatches reveals that failing doctors routinely slip through the system. We've been filming secretly in GP practices and have uncovered concerning evidence of misdiagnosis by doctors who have failed in the past, but are still practicing

videos.title: North Korea: Life Inside the Secret State
videos.overview: North Koreans are breaking down the barriers of the gulag state. Following covert filmmakers, this doc shows real life under the new leader Kim Jong Un, highlighting the contrasting ox-drawn farms to the glittering life of the elite in Pyongyang. The starving children on the streets are of artificial food shortages engendered by corruption. See how USBs, cell phones and DVDs from the South are transforming North Koreans' views of their world.

videos.title: What's Your Pension Really Worth?
videos.overview: Michael Buerk investigates the pensions crises facing us all. As the cost of living rises faster than many pay packets and life expectancy increases, he asks what your pension is really worth?

videos.title: Britain's Big Fat Bill
videos.overview: As Britain gets fatter, Channel 4 Dispatches investigates what the real cost is to the nation. The programme follows the treatment of some of Britain's morbidly obese patients to reveal the spiralling cost to the NHS.

videos.title: Secrets of the Discount Stores
videos.overview: Lifts the lid on the shops promising luxury labels for less.

videos.title: Are You Addicted to Sugar?
videos.overview: Will eating less really help? Experts say that the real problem lies in the quantity of sugar hidden in the food we eat. So is Britain addicted to sugar?

videos.title: Children on the Frontline
videos.overview: The children of Syria are often the forgotten victims in the ongoing civil war. More than 11,000 children have been killed and over a million are now refugees.

videos.title: Floods: Your Money Down the Drain
videos.overview: The floods that recently hit Britain have caused misery for thousands, but do you know what's actually in the flood water that has engulfed our towns and streets?

videos.title: Hunted
videos.overview: On the eve of the Sochi Winter Olympics, Russia is officially welcoming gay athletes and spectators. But in a country where it's thought only 1% of gay people dare to live completely openly, it appears to be a hollow gesture.

videos.title: Benefits Britain: The Bedroom Tax
videos.overview: Of the welfare changes brought in by the coalition gov't, the so-called Bedroom Tax is perhaps most controversial. Thousands of people around the country have had their housing benefit reduced because of a spare room in their house or flat

videos.title: A&E's Missing Millions
videos.overview: With Accident and Emergency Departments under pressure, Dispatches investigates the cost and consequence of financial penalties imposed on hospitals when government targets to treat emergency cases are missed.

videos.title: Secrets of Your Credit Rating
videos.overview: A bad credit rating can affect your chances of getting access to bank loans, mortgages and even mobile phone contracts. But how accurate is the information used to compile your credit report, and what happens if there is a mistake in it?

videos.title: Undercover: Hate on the Terraces
videos.overview: Reporter Morland Sanders' investigation exposes how some supporters take part in systematic and flagrant homophobic chanting. It also raises serious concerns about the police's response to racism and homophobia.

videos.title: Food: What's Really in your Trolley?
videos.overview: Morland Sanders investigates the criminal gangs moving into the food business, the profits that can be made by substituting fake foods, and how the authorities are struggling to battle the rising tide of food fraud.

videos.title: Amanda Holden: Exposing Hospital Heartache
videos.overview: Holden investigates the treatment of some couples whose pregnancies end in failure. Mothers who tell her their experiences in the aftermath of their loss left a great deal to be desired, and seeks answers from those in authority in the NHS

videos.title: The Truth About Low Fat Food
videos.overview: Do you know how skinny your muffin is? Or what's in your low-fat yoghurt? As the public try to grapple with confusing messages about what's best to eat, Dispatches investigates how the food industry has reacted to our fear of fat.

videos.title: Policemen Behaving Badly
videos.overview: It's called the Police Federation - the police's union - and it represents the interests of 131,000 officers across the country. They never break ranks, and no one ever speaks out; until now.

videos.title: Tricks of the Junk Food Business
videos.overview: Do you know when an advert is really an advert? Are you sure that the game you're playing isn't trying to make you buy something? When it comes to protecting our children from sugary food, the world of online advertising is a new frontier.

videos.title: Breadline Kids
videos.overview: Over 300,000 children were given food aid in the UK last year. Politicians continue to argue about why many kids are experiencing food poverty, Dispatches asked three children to reveal how it feels when the cupboards are sometimes bare.

videos.title: Secrets of the Police
videos.overview: 'Plebgate' and Hillsborough have made many in Britain question the honesty and integrity of some of our police officers. Now Dispatches investigates how they handle one of the most sensitive areas of policing: complaints of police racism.

videos.title: How to Fix a Football Match
videos.overview: As World Cup fever grips the globe, Morland Sanders investigates the dark side of the international game. Dispatches goes undercover to expose world football's problem with match-fixing.

videos.title: The Cost of Cheap Alcohol
videos.overview: There is concern that the wide availability of cheap alcohol may have a darker side. Alcohol-related crime, violence, accidents and disease are costing the country billions of pounds a year.

videos.title: The Great British Break-up?
videos.overview: In September Scotland will go to the polls to vote on independence, people south of the border can only watch and wait. Antony Barnett goes on the campaign trail of both sides to investigate claims of dubious tactics and misinformation.

videos.title: Faith Schools Undercover: No Clapping in Class
videos.overview: As the government is about to publish its report on the 'Trojan Horse' affair in Birmingham, Dispatches goes undercover to question the role of faith communities in our schools.

videos.title: Murder in the Sky: Flight MH17
videos.overview: On July 16 a flight full of tourists, travellers and families took off from Amsterdam en-route to Malaysia. Four hours after take-off the Boeing 777 was flying above war-torn eastern Ukraine when it lost all contact with flight control.

videos.title: Supermarket Wars
videos.overview: The era of domination by the big 4 - Tesco, Sainsbury's, Morrisons and Asda - is waning. Profits are slumping and online shopping is transforming the market. While the big 4 struggle, discounters like Aldi and Lidl are booming.

videos.title: Supermarkets: The Real Price of Cheap Food
videos.overview: Morland Sanders lifts the lid on key supermarket suppliers. From field to factory, Dispatches examines hygiene, health and safety and the reality of life on minimum-wage, minimum-security, ultra-flexible contracts.

videos.title: How to Stop Your Nuisance Calls
videos.overview: Fed up with receiving repeated telephone calls asking for charity donations? Ever wondered why you keep getting called despite saying no? How did they get your number? Dispatches goes undercover to find the answers.

videos.title: Are You Addicted to Your Doctor?
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates those who are over-using our health system, from the anxious woman who calls an ambulance 20 times a year, to the young mums who head to A&E with minor ailments and illnesses.

videos.title: Nigeria's Hidden War
videos.overview: Dispatches reveals a dark side to Nigeria's on-going war against Islamist terror groups such as Boko Haram: a campaign by the Nigerian security forces against civilians so brutal it could be classed a war crime.

videos.title: Rice: How Safe Is Our Food?
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates claims by some leading experts that some types of commonly consumed rice contain worryingly high levels of naturally occurring arsenic

videos.title: How the Rich Get Richer
videos.overview: Fraser Nelson, the editor of The Spectator magazine, explores the growing inequality in British society. In areas such as education, prospects and life expectancy there's a growing gulf between the haves and have not's.

videos.title: How to Break Into Britain (II)
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover inside the makeshift camps around Calais to investigate the criminal gangs that are making big money by smuggling illegal immigrants into Britain.

videos.title: The British Property Boom
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates the consequences of rapid house price rises for buyers, sellers and communities and examines how the property boom of 2014 is changing the face of our towns and cities.

videos.title: How to Blow Your Pension
videos.overview: Changes to the rules regarding private pension withdrawals mean some retirees are planning on raiding their pension pot to take luxury holidays or pay of debts. Michael Buerk asks if the state will be left to pick up the pieces.

videos.title: Low Pay Britain
videos.overview: As parties launch their General Election campaigns focusing on Britain's economic recovery, Morland Sanders investigates the reality of the workforce today and shows how major companies are saving money on wages and taxes.

videos.title: The Great Car Con
videos.overview: British motorists were told that diesel would be the cheap, environmentally friendly fuel of the future but growing concerns over harmful emissions and the reliability of emissions tests have led to calls for surcharges or bans on diesels.

videos.title: Secrets Of The Parking Wardens
videos.overview: The number of parking tickets issues by private firms has rocketed since 2007, with more than 2.5 million issued annually. Reporter Antony Barnett goes undercover to investigate why complaints against them have also grown.

videos.title: Politicians for Hire II
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover once again to expose the cash-for-access scandal of MP's accepting fees to provide access to government. This time two former Foreign Secretaries are the target of the sting operation.

videos.title: Britain's Benefits Crackdown
videos.overview: The Government has vowed to clampdown on benefit claimants and has introduced a new system of sanctions against those it thinks are abusing the system. Liz MacKean meets those hit by the new penalties.

videos.title: Benefits Britain: Universal Credit
videos.overview: The Government is introducing the new Universal Credit in the biggest welfare reform in a generation. It is claimed the new benefit is helping people back into work, Dispatches investigates claims the new system is a shambles.

videos.title: Britain's Defence Squeeze
videos.overview: In the wake of significant cuts to the UK defence budget, Morland Sanders asks if the nation is still able to defend itself adequately in the face of a growing range of threats.

videos.title: How to Buy a Meeting with a Minister
videos.overview: In the run-up to the General Election, Antony Barnett presents an undercover investigation into the way in which donors can pay to attend social functions with government ministers to discuss "issues".

videos.title: The Secrets of Sports Direct
videos.overview: How does Sports Direct sell it's trainers and clothing so cheaply? Harry Wallop examines the hidden costs behind the success of the high street store who have been accused of "reprehensible" business practices.

videos.title: Trains: Are You Paying Too Much?
videos.overview: As rail passenger numbers hit an all-time high Morland Sanders goes undercover inside one of Britain's biggest rail operators to examine the key problems of ticket pricing, overcrowding and compensation claims.

videos.title: Where to Save Your Money
videos.overview: Interest rates are at their lowest in 300 years, Channel 4 News Business Editor Siobhan Kennedy reports on the problems facing savers and examines some of the options available to them in a confusing market.

videos.title: Exams: Cheating the System?
videos.overview: Seyi Rhodes examines how some schools and pupils are coping with the stresses and strains of the exam system by bending the rules. He speaks to 'whistleblowers' within the education sector who reveal some of the tactics used.

videos.title: The Great British Property Divide
videos.overview: From million-pound flats to so-called "poor doors", Morland Sanders investigates how rising house prices can transform communities and the impact the right-to-buy law will have on the property divide.

videos.title: Salt: Are You Eating Too Much?
videos.overview: Amidst calls to reduce the amount of salt consumed in our diets, reporter Tazeen Ahmad uncovers disturbing evidence that the labelling of salt content on our food is far from always accurate

videos.title: Kids in Crisis
videos.overview: In this hour-long special report Dispatches meets with four families who all have children who suffer from mental illness. The lack of local residential care means these youngsters have to be separated from their loved ones to seek help.

videos.title: How Councils Blow Your Millions
videos.overview: Dispatches reporter Antony Barnett investigates the secretive deals that British local authorities have done with banks around the world that are costing the UK taxpayer millions of pounds.

videos.title: Pensions and the Price of Growing Old
Escape from Isis
videos.overview: In this one-hour special report Dispatches reveals the brutal regime millions of women face when living under the control of the so-called Islamic State and meets a dedicated team of men risking their lives to free them.

videos.title: Hunted: Gay and Afraid
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates the well-funded global network of groups that are supporting a new wave of anti-gay legislation around the world including America's "World Congress of Families".

videos.title: Aldi's Supermarket Secrets
videos.overview: Discount supermarket chain Aldi continues to go from strength to strength, recently overtaking Waitrose as Britain's sixth biggest supermarket. Morland Sanders goes undercover to see if quality and service are suffering.

videos.title: How to Stop Your Nuisance Calls II
videos.overview: Millions of people are plagued by nuisance callers trying to sell them things that they don't want, Dispatches goes undercover to investigate the cold calling industry and meets the people fighting back.

videos.title: Britain's Nightmare New Homes
videos.overview: With the Government pledging to build a million new homes across Britain by 2020, Seyi Rhodes investigates if the rush to build so many new houses is having an impact on the quality these homes.

videos.title: Low Pay Britain II
videos.overview: The Government has promised to help create 3 million apprenticeships alongside a new national living wage. Dispatches investigates claims that some employers are wasting public money and abusing the trust placed in them.

videos.title: How the Monarchy Can Make You Millions
videos.overview: Around 800 companies hold royal warrants and it is thought that they make an extra £4 billion a year because of it. With the stakes so high, Antony Barnett examines the system of granting royal approval.

videos.title: The Children Who Beat Ebola
videos.overview: The remarkable story of five extraordinary children in Sierra Leone who fought off the deadly Ebola virus and overcame loss and social stigma to rebuild their lives.

videos.title: Where's My Missing Mail?
videos.overview: Morland Sanders presents an undercover report into parcel delivery companies where missing items, broken gifts and late deliveries are all becoming a growing problem.

videos.title: How the Rich Avoid Tax
videos.overview: Actor Greg Wise secretly records his meetings with tax planners, who reveal to him a range of legal tax avoidance schemes that are available to the rich and famous.

videos.title: 999: Where's My Ambulance?
videos.overview: Demand for ambulance services are at an all-time high and many trusts are struggling to meet response time targets. Morland Sanders investigates why there is such a demand and what can be done to meet it.

videos.title: Dirty Secrets: What's Really in Our Air?
videos.overview: People are breathing in more harmful pollutants than official figures suggest. Morland Sanders uses high-tech monitoring equipment to identify hidden pollution hot-spots and talks to experts about the effect this is having.

videos.title: How To Be A Council House Millionaire
videos.overview: The Government plans to extend the right-to-buy scheme to housing association tenants, Antony Barnett looks at who will be the winners and losers. Includes undercover filming at one of the property companies hoping to benefit.

videos.title: Housing Benefit Millionaires
videos.overview: Antony Barnett reports on the rogue private landlords who are exploiting the housing benefit system by renting out sub-standard accommodation to tenants in receipt of the benefit, often putting lives at risk.

videos.title: Secrets of Cadbury
videos.overview: 6 years ago British confectioner Cadbury was taken over by the U.S. food giant Kraft in one of the most talked about takeovers of recent years. Harry Wallop reports on the controversies that have plagued the company since then.

videos.title: Britain's Pensioner Care Scandal
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover to examine the level of care that some of Britain's most vulnerable pensioners receive from a home care industry under pressure from rising costs and cuts to budgets.

videos.title: The Great Benefits Row
videos.overview: Former Paralympian Ade Adepitan reports on the row over welfare cuts that has rocked the Government and prompted Iain Duncan Smith to resign as Secretary of State for Work and Pensions.

videos.title: Isis and the Missing Treasures
