videos.overview: Simon Cox investigates the UK trade in antiquities that have been looted from areas under the control of ISIS, examining this lucrative business and testing the laws designed to regulate it.

videos.title: The Truth About Cheap Flights
videos.overview: Harry Wallop presents an undercover report revealing the secrets of one of the major players in the travel industry. Dispatches asks if really low fares are all that they seem and the best deal for passengers.

videos.title: Undercover: Inside Britain's Children's Services
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover inside Birmingham City Council's Children's Services Department, Britain's largest, which was described in 2013 by Ofsted's Chief Inspector as a national disgrace.

videos.title: Are You Owed a Pay Rise?
videos.overview: Morland Sanders investigates the new National Living Wage. Despite only being introduced in April 2016 it has already caused controversy amid reports that employers are cutting other staff benefits.

videos.title: Racist Britain
videos.overview: Seyi Rhodes investigates the alarming rise in the number of hate crimes being reported in the wake of Britain's vote to leave the European Union, containing shocking footage of abuse and attacks.

videos.title: Is Your Pension Safe?
videos.overview: Reporter Shaunagh Connaire investigates the increasing pressures on the UK pension industry post-Brexit and asks if more companies will find themselves struggling to meet their pension commitments.

videos.title: How School Bosses Spend Your Millions
videos.overview: Antony Barnett investigates the Government push to massively expand the academy school system, discovering the large salaries and extremely generous expenses and perks some staff receive.

videos.title: How Safe Is Your Car?
videos.overview: Morland Sanders investigates whether manufacturers and testers can be trusted over car safety and examines if more could be done to protect drivers and passengers.

videos.title: Brexit: Who'll Do Your Job Now?
videos.overview: Morland Sanders asks who will take Britain's low-skilled jobs - picking food, cleaning toilets and packing parcels if EU workers are no longer plentiful and looks into reports of a shadowy North Korean workforce in Europe.

videos.title: The Great Housing Scandal
videos.overview: Harry Wallop investigates the housing shortage in Britain and in particular the Government sell-off of state-owned land to build housing on. He discovers that the land was undersold and few houses built on it.

videos.title: The Battle for the Labour Party
videos.overview: Antony Barnett investigates the current state of the Labour Party in the run-up to the result of the leadership contest. He also investigates Momentum and those seeking to influence the party.

videos.title: Undercover: Britain's Abortion Extremists
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates the anti-abortion movement in the UK

videos.title: Britain's Wealth Gap
videos.overview: The increasing wealth gap between the young and the old has become one of the defining features of our times. Fraser Nelson, editor of The Spectator magazine, reveals the extent of the gap and its causes.

videos.title: Living With Nightmare Neighbours
videos.overview: The Government promised to fix so-called "Neighbours From Hell" with it's new Troubled Families Programme. Morland Sanders investigates if the scheme has really worked, meeting families that say it has had little impact.

videos.title: Addicted to Spending
videos.overview: From online shopping to contactless payment, it has never been easier to spend money. Reporter Morland Sanders meets those struggling to control their spending habits and the companies profiting from those debts.

videos.title: The Secret Plan to Save Fat Britain
videos.overview: British men are the fattest in Europe, British women the second fattest and our children are getting fatter, younger. Antony Barnett investigates why the Government's plans to tackle childhood obesity seem to have been watered down.

videos.title: Britain's Homebuilding Scandal
videos.overview: A shortage of housing in Britain has left many struggling to get onto the property ladder. Councils have granted planning permission to big building companies, so why are so few new houses being built? Dispatches investigates.

videos.title: The World According to President Trump
videos.overview: Channel 4 Dispatches Editor George Waldrum has commissioned a Dispatches special from ITN Productions in response to the results of the US General Election - The World According to President Trump. What will a President Trump really do? Will he really ban all Muslims? Build a wall? Pal up to Putin? Smash Isis? How scared should we be? Will he back down from his campaign pledges? In this special film, Matt Frei speaks to those who know and attempts to get to the bottom of Trump's policies and future agenda as President of the United States. Commissioning editor George Waldrum says, "We have never seen anything like it before, or possibly ever will again. The controversy surrounding the election has been remarkable and it is a great opportunity to continue the coverage and analysis on Channel 4. Matt Frei has been at the heart of the election coverage and can provide great insight into the aftermath of the election."

videos.title: President Trump's Dirty Secrets
videos.overview: Reporter Antony Barnett investigates some of the controversial figures surrounding Donald Trump and how their links to powerful corporations could have far-reaching consequences beyond America.

videos.title: Undercover: Britain's Cheap Clothes (1)
videos.overview: Tazeen Ahmad follows up her 2010 report into working conditions inside factories which are making clothing for major brand labels to see if life has improved for the workers making our clothes.

videos.title: Undercover: Britain's Cheap Clothes (2)
videos.overview: In the second documentary investigating the resurgent UK textile industry, Dispatches goes undercover to follow the next stage of the industry - inside the vast distribution warehouses servicing our online orders.

videos.title: Undercover: Britain's Homeless Scandal
videos.overview: With councils across England and Wales struggling to meet the demand for emergency housing, Jackie Long investigates the impact on homeless women trying to escape life on the streets.

videos.title: Supermarkets: Brexit and Your Shrinking Shop
videos.overview: Harry Wallop reveals which of Britain's favourite brands have been affected by the Brexit vote and looks at how the imposition of European import taxes cold affect the cost of shopping in the UK.

videos.title: Inside Britain's Airports
videos.overview: Each year Britain's airports rake in more than 4 billion pounds, mostly from the plethora of shops in their terminals. Reporter Harry Wallop investigates if passengers are getting a good deal.

videos.title: Under Lock and Key
videos.overview: Thousands of young people with learning disabilities and autism are still being locked up in hospital despite promises made by the government. This special report highlights the lack of bespoke care to meet their needs.

videos.title: Brexit: Crisis on the Wards
videos.overview: This winter, the NHS has suffered one of the most challenging periods in its history. Morland Sanders investigates if the Brexit vote is going to deliver an even bigger problem as staff from EU countries leave.

videos.title: Britain's Benefit Families
videos.overview: Seyi Rhodes investigates benefit reforms by speaking to claimants who have had their housing benefit capped, landlords who can no longer accept claimants as tenants and local councils left to pick up the pieces.

videos.title: Syria's Disappeared: The Case Against Assad
videos.overview: Documentary investigating how tens of thousands of men, women and children have been disappeared by the Assad regime into a network of clandestine detention centers.

videos.title: Secrets of Coca-Cola
videos.overview: Antony Barnett reveals the response of the global soft drinks giant to the UK Government's sugar-tax and leaked e-mails which show the corporation is gathering scientists and academics to challenge the legislation.

videos.title: President Trump: How Scared Should We Be?
videos.overview: Abigail Austen travels to the US to assess what the age of Trump means for the rest of the world, and how serious a threat some of his policies pose to peace and stability around the globe.

videos.title: Isis and the Battle for Iraq
videos.overview: Emmy-award winning journalist Ramita Navai reveals the other side of the war against ISIS in Iraq, looking at allegations of torture, execution and sectarian cleansing of Sunni refugees by Shia militias.

videos.title: Trump, The Doctor and The Vaccine Scandal
videos.overview: With fear of vaccination resurgent in the United States, Cathy Newman reveals the role played by disgraced British doctor Andrew Wakefield in the Trump administration.

videos.title: Bupa Care Homes Undercover
videos.overview: Undercover filming uncovers the specialist dementia care homes for the elderly operated by the UK's largest private medical business BUPA amid allegations of neglect and abuse of patients

videos.title: Brexit - How to Get a British Passport
videos.overview: Reporter Datshiane Navanayagam investigates the many hurdles and costs that people face applying for British citizenship and passports - including large numbers of children born and raised in Britain.

videos.title: Secrets of Your Cruise
videos.overview: Tazeen Ahmad goes undercover as a passenger to investigate the impact that some cruise ships could be having on the environment and public health

videos.title: Secrets of Britain's New Homes
videos.overview: Antony Barnett investigates why so few new homes are being built across Britain and examines links between the property industry and the Government.

videos.title: Wasting Away: The Truth About Anorexia
videos.overview: Mark Austin and his daughter Maddy explore the devastating effects of eating disorders, the availability of suitable care and talk to patients, their families, Prince William of Wales and Health Secretary Jeremy Hunt.

videos.title: Secrets of Your New Car
videos.overview: As concern once again grows around household debt, Dispatches investigates car finance. Undercover filming exposes questionable sales tactics and confusing advice given to customers.

videos.title: How to Get a Pay Rise
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates low wage growth, asking who is responsible for wage stagnation and provides a masterclass on how to get a pay rise.

videos.title: Trump & Russia: Sex, Spies and Scandal
videos.overview: A year after one of the greatest political upsets of all time, Matt Frei travels to Moscow and Washington to find out more about the alleged conspiracy between Donald Trump and Russia.

videos.title: Who Deserves a Pay Rise?
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates what life is like for front-line public sector workers following seven years of pay freezes and pay caps, revealing how far salaries have fallen in real terms.

videos.title: Is Britain Full?
videos.overview: Michael Buerk investigates whether the country can cope with current levels of immigration and the impact of internal migration on over and under populated areas.

videos.title: Trouble on the Trains
videos.overview: Morland Sanders gains access to undercover footage from British Transport Police that exposes the bad behaviour of football-fans on the UK's rail network as they bring offensive chants from the stadiums to the carriages.

videos.title: The Fight For Mosul
videos.overview: Follows the experiences of five young Iraqi Special Forces soldiers tasked with fighting ISIS in Mosul who are haunted by what they've seen and what they've done.

videos.title: The Great Housing Scandal
videos.overview: Following the Grenfell Tower fire, the Prime Minister dedicated her premiership to fixing Britain's broken housing market. Do some of her government's actions contradict that pledge?

videos.title: How to Avoid the Dementia Tax
videos.overview: Tazeen Ahmad investigates the so-called "dementia tax". Why do some dementia sufferers have to sell their home to pay for care, while others gain access to NHS funding?

videos.title: Politicians for Hire: Cashing in on Brexit
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover posing as representatives of a Chinese company to investigate how politicians, including former cabinet ministers, are looking to make money by advising businesses about Brexit.

videos.title: Undercover in Premier Inn
videos.overview: A reporter goes undercover as an agency housekeeper working at a Premier Inn hotel in central London and discovers some uncomfortable truths about what it is like for some of the people working there.

videos.title: Football's Wall of Silence
videos.overview: In an Al Jazeera investigation, Reporter Deboarah Davies reveals how former youth football coach Barry Bennell spent his days coaching children and nights abusing them.

videos.title: Undercover: Inside the Priory
videos.overview: Faced with a shortage of places to treat mental health patients, the NHS is placing patients in private hospitals. Dispatches goes undercover inside one of the American-owned Priory Group's hospitals to investigate.

videos.title: Britain's University Spending Scandal
videos.overview: At a time when students are graduating up to 58,000 pounds in debt and university staff are protesting about cuts to their pensions, Dispatches investigates the expenses of Britain's top universities.

videos.title: The Week Britain Froze
videos.overview: The Week Britain Froze examines the causes of the Beast from the East, tells extraordinary stories of human courage, and asks if this freezing weather is a sign of things to come.

videos.title: Undercover: Who's Policing Your Bank?
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover to discover if the UK's Financial Ombudsman acts in favour of banks and against their customers.

videos.title: The Truth About Your Pay
videos.overview: With the deadline for companies to disclose their gender pay gap approaching, reporter Tazeen Ahmad reveals how the figures presented may not be all that they seem.

videos.title: Who Speaks for British Muslims?
videos.overview: Across Britain the police, government agencies and other public bodies have been reaching out to Muslim groups in the fight against extremism - but how much do they know about some of these groups?

videos.title: Russian Spy Assassins: The Salisbury Attack
videos.overview: Matt Frei examines former Russian double agent Sergei Skripal's past - and the murky world of espionage, politics and crime - to find potential motives for his poisoning in Salisbury.

videos.title: Britain's Diesel Scandal
videos.overview: An undercover investigation into how British hauliers are using hi-tech cheat devices and computer hacking to disable the emissions controls on their lorries saving them money but worsening air quality.

videos.title: The True Cost of Green Energy
videos.overview: An investigation of the government-subsidised renewable energy industry turning trees into fuel, asking whether burning wood is really a more environmentally friendly alternative to burning coal.

videos.title: Britain's Benefits Crisis
videos.overview: Morland Sanders asks if the changes made to the Universal Credit system have forced some people to become homeless and to turn to food banks for support and if the nationwide roll-out of the changes should be halted.

videos.title: Myanmar's Killing Fields
videos.overview: For the past five years an undercover network of Rohingya activists have been risking their lives to secretly film evidence of years of repression, violence and mass murder by the authorities in Myanmar.

videos.title: After Grenfell, How Safe Are We?
videos.overview: A year on from the Grenfell Tower disaster Ed Howker investigates claims that even after the Hackitt Review of building regulations Britain's tower blocks are still not safe.

videos.title: Getting Rich From the Housing Crisis
videos.overview: Britain faces a major housing shortage so how is it that some of those who are responsible for providing the social housing that is so desperately needed seem to be doing so well out of the crisis?

videos.title: Inside Facebook: Secrets of the Social Network
videos.overview: Dispatches goes undercover in the secretive world of the people who decide what can and can't be posted on Facebook, exploring how their decisions are made and the impact they have on users.

videos.title: Plot to Kill: Britain's Neo-Nazi Terrorists
videos.overview: With exclusive access to the secretive world of Britain's new neo-Nazis, Dispatches tells the inside story of a far-right terrorist plot to murder an MP, and how the plan was betrayed to the police.

videos.title: Homeless and Working
videos.overview: Datshiane Navanayagam goes behind the scenes at two homeless shelters in London to reveal the growing number of people who are in work but are unable to afford high private rents in a low wage economy.

videos.title: Breastfeeding Uncovered
videos.overview: Journalist and television presenter Kate Quilton investigates why Britain has some of the worst breastfeeding rates in the world and also explores some of the scientific evidence for the benefits of breast milk.

videos.title: How to lose Seven Billion Pounds
videos.overview: Liam Halligan reveals the story behind the collapse of Carillion, the vast British company built on billions of pounds of public money and that imploded in January 2018.

videos.title: Lawless Britain: Where are the Police?
videos.overview: An increasing number of victims of crime are claiming that the police are not fully investigating their cases, while police cite a lack of resources. Are we entering a new era of policing?

videos.title: Witness Intimidation Revealed: Stitches For Snitches
videos.overview: Livvy Haydock explores the dark world of online witness intimidation, meeting those who threaten 'snitches' and the families of witnesses who paid the price for telling the truth in court.

videos.title: Cannabis: Time to End the Ban?
videos.overview: Over 2 million people smoke cannabis in the UK. Some police forces no longer prosecute for possession. Canada and several American States have legalised it. So should the UK follow suit?

videos.title: Born on the Breadline
videos.overview: Examines the growing need for baby banks in the UK and meets the working parents who are turning to them to provide their young children with nappies, clothes, toys and cots.

videos.title: North Korea: Life Inside the Secret State
videos.overview: North Korean citizens reveal what life is like for the 24 million people who live in the world's most secretive country, where the state controls every aspect of their life.

videos.title: The Truth About Vegans
videos.overview: Morland Sanders investigates the increasing popularity of veganism. It's better for your health, the environment and animals but why do some activists resort to extreme tactics to promote it?

videos.title: Skipping School: Britain's Invisible Kids
videos.overview: A report on the increasing number of children being educated at home in the UK, investigating the reasons behind this dramatic rise and the impact it is having on young people.

videos.title: HS2: The Great Train Robbery
videos.overview: Liam Halligan reports on the multi-billion-pound high-speed rail line. With costs soaring should it be scrapped and the money spent on improving local rail networks instead.

videos.title: Grenfell: Did the Fire Brigade Fail?
videos.overview: An examination of the London Fire Brigade's response to the Grenfell Tower fire in light of new evidence from the public inquiry and interviews with firefighters and survivors.

videos.title: Safe at Last: Inside a Women's Refuge
videos.overview: In a television first, cameras are allowed inside a women's refuge to follow the stories of women who are fleeing from violent partners, and who have agreed to be identified.

videos.title: Britain's Knife Crisis: Young, Armed and Dangerous
videos.overview: Former Metropolitan Police Commissioner Bernard Hogan-Howe examines why there has been a rise in knife crime and asks what Britain needs to do to get the problem under control.

videos.title: The Brexit Millionaires
videos.overview: Antony Barnett investigates those who have profited from the uncertainty since the UK's referendum on membership of the EU, including politicians, consultancy firms and those who 'shorted' against Britain.

videos.title: Great Formula Milk Scandal
videos.overview: New mum Kate Quilton investigates if formula milk is being fairly priced and if claims made for its benefits are unbiased and scientifically proven.

videos.title: New Landlords From Hell
videos.overview: A year-long investigation by Datshiane Navanayagam reveals the shocking conditions endured by tenants of one of the UK's largest housing associations, Sanctuary Housing, and the effect on vulnerable people's health.

videos.title: Britain's Hidden War
videos.overview: With BAE Systems keeping Saudi jets in the air and British military officers working in the Saudi Air Operations Centre, Sue Turton investigates the extent to which the war in Yemen is made in Britian.

videos.title: When the Immigrants Leave
videos.overview: Ahead of Brexit, reporter Seyi Rhodes explores how a lack of migrant workers from the European Union could affect agriculture, social care and health-care in Britain.

videos.title: Jeremy Kyle: TV on Trial
videos.overview: In the wake of the cancellation of The Jeremy Kyle Show following the death of a guest who appeared on the programme, Morland Sanders investigates what lies behind the headlines, what went wrong and who might be to blame.

videos.title: The Truth About Chlorinated Chicken
videos.overview: With chemically-washed chicken being pushed as part of a post-Brexit Anglo-American trade deal this undercover report goes inside an American poultry processing plant to investigate the practice.

videos.title: Britain's Toxic Air Scandal
videos.overview: 1 in 3 children in the UK is growing up inhaling unsafe levels of air pollution. Reporter Morland Sanders reveals it's not just exhausts producing dangerous emissions with toxins coming off every vehicle - even electric ones.

videos.title: How Safe Are Your Medicines?
videos.overview: In 2014 millions of pounds worth of medicines were stolen from Italian hospitals then sold by bogus drugs wholesalers - some of which ended up in the NHS supply chain. Antony Barnett investigates.

videos.title: Britain's Breast Implant Scandal
videos.overview: Abbie Eastwood investigates whether breast implants are making women ill, or worse still causing cancer.

videos.title: Officer Down - Police Under Attack
videos.overview: Former police officer Dan Neal investigates the worrying rise in the number of assaults on police officers as they go about their job.

videos.title: Battle for the Tory Party
videos.overview: As members of the Conservative Party choose our next Prime Minister, Gary Gibbon examines who really holds the reins of power.

videos.title: Britain's New Build Scandal
videos.overview: Liam Halligan investigates claims of shoddy standards, poor customer care and excessive profits at Britain's second biggest - and most profitable - house-builder, Persimmon.

videos.title: £2 Million Passport: Welcome to Britain
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates the 'golden visa' scheme, which offers British residency to wealthy foreign nationals who are willing to invest two million pounds in the UK.

videos.title: Young, British and Depressed
videos.overview: "We're promoting the idea that it's ok to have a mental health problem - but it's made us afraid of our emotions." Dispatches investigates claims that de-stigmatisation campaigns are having unintended negative consequences, leading some to wrongly believe they have problems with their mental health.

videos.title: Sex, Drugs and Murder
videos.overview: A special investigation into the epidemic use of the drug GHB in the gay community, where users are vulnerable to overdosing and sexual abuse.

videos.title: The Prince and the Paedophile
videos.overview: Cathy Newman investigates the friendship between Andrew Mountbatten-Windsor and paedophile Jeffrey Epstein amid accusations that the Prince slept with a 17-year-old girl supplied by Epstein.

videos.title: Trump's Plan for the NHS
videos.overview: How Trump's proposed trade agreement with post-Brexit Britain could cost the NHS billions.

videos.title: Puppet Masters: The Men Who Really Run Britain
videos.overview: Gary Gibbon examines the role played by Dominic Cummings and Seumas Milne the controversial political advisors to Boris Johnson and Jeremy Corbyn.

videos.title: The Secrets of Amazon
videos.overview: Sophie Morgan explores some of the complaints about the global company, including working conditions, selling toxic toys and pro-anorexia books, tax avoidance and selling on personal data.

videos.title: Born Homeless
videos.overview: Explores the issue of pregnant women who find themselves with no place to call home, and conducts an exclusive survey of midwives to get a sense of the scale of the problem.

videos.title: Growing Up Poor: Britain's Breadline Kids
videos.overview: In Britain, 4.1 million children are growing up in poverty. This special report follows three families to show what life is like if there's not enough money for life's essentials.

videos.title: Britain's Child Drug Runners
videos.overview: Children as young as seven are being groomed to sell drugs for 'county lines' drugs gangs in towns and villages all over the UK. This documentary follows four young people trapped in this world.

videos.title: The Secrets of Big Tobacco: Has Philip Morris International Really Given Up Smoking?
videos.overview: Philip Morris International has said it wants a smoke-free future and offers so-called reduced-risk alternatives. But at the same as its campaign promotes this in the UK it continues to sell billions of cigarettes across the world.

videos.title: Starbucks & Nespresso: The Truth About Your Coffee
videos.overview: Antony Barnett travels to Guatemala where he learns that young children are working long hours in gruelling conditions picking coffee beans that supply Starbucks and Nespresso.

videos.title: Celebs for Sale: The Great Charity Scandal
videos.overview: Antony Barnett goes undercover to reveal how some of the most famous people in Britain are profiting from the work they do for charity

videos.title: Britain's Train Hell
videos.overview: As Britain's rail commuters face rising fares, delays and overcrowding, the Government plans a high speed train that won't run until 2040. How do we fix our railways now?

videos.title: Sex, Money & Power: The Dirty Secrets of Davos
videos.overview: Caitlin Brown investigates allegations of sexism and harassment in Davos at the annual summit of world leaders and businessmen, hearing from women who are fed up with their treatment by men.

videos.title: Coronavirus: How Britain Is Changing
videos.overview: A look at how the coronavirus outbreak is changing Britain in the long term, for better or worse, from a reduction in pollution to economic policy.

videos.title: The Truth About Traveller Crime
videos.overview: Anja Popp goes in search of the truth about crimes linked to traveller sites. She talks to members of the public who have experienced crime waves and intimidation, goes out on patrol with police dealing with rural incidents and hears from travellers and their advocates, who say they suffer prejudice and attack.

videos.title: Britain's Coronavirus Catastrophe: Did the Government Get it Wrong?
videos.overview: With Britain's Covid death rate one of the world's highest, Antony Barnett examines the evidence and asks did the government get it wrong?

videos.title: Dirty Secrets of American Food: Coming to a Supermarket Near You?
videos.overview: Morland Sanders investigates the American food that could be coming to Britain soon as part of a post-Brexit trade deal. with exclusive lab results revealing levels of dangerous bacteria on US supermarket meat. He looks at the widespread use of pesticides and hormones currently banned in the UK, and uncovers animal welfare concerns and declining hygiene standards in American food production, as well as fears the deal could harm the British farming industry.

videos.title: Trump's Coronavirus Catastrophe
videos.overview: After months of conversations with White House advisors insiders, whistleblowers, politicians, scientists, and Trump supporters, Matt Frei investigates the President's performance during the pandemic.

videos.title: How Safe Is Going Out?
videos.overview: As Britain's service industry battles to survive Covid-19, Morland Sanders investigates the promises made by hotels, trains and pubs of 'deep cleans' and 'enhanced hygiene practices'.

videos.title: American Nightmare: Trump's Breadline Kids
videos.overview: On the eve of the US Presidential election, with the backdrop of Covid-19 and racial tension, this documentary examines the experience of poverty through the eyes of three children in the battleground state of Ohio.

videos.title: Britain's Covid Job Crisis
videos.overview: As the furlough scheme ends, cameras follow a minimum-wage paying job vacancy at a Manchester restaurant, which attracts almost 1000 applicants as unemployment rates spiral.

videos.title: Is Your Online Habit Killing the Planet?
videos.overview: Sophie Morgan investigates the carbon footprint of the tech industry, as she discovers some shocking truths about the hidden cost of our online habits.

videos.title: Lockdown Chaos: How the Government Lost Control
videos.overview: As most of the UK goes back into lockdown, Antony Barnett reveals what went wrong, how the government lost control, and the companies making millions from the pandemic.

videos.title: Coronavirus Vaccine: Is It Safe?
videos.overview: With the UK the first to approve and roll-out a coronavirus vaccine, Matt Frei asks how have we managed so quickly and just how safe is it? Is it the shot in the arm to get Britain moving again?

videos.title: Deep Fakes: Can You Trust Your Eyes?
Britain's £400bn COVID Bill: Who Will Pay?
videos.overview: Britain in lockdown faces the worst economic nosedive in 300 years. Liam Halligan looks at the financial cost of the pandemic and what it could mean for our futures.

videos.title: Condition Critical - One Doctor's Story
videos.overview: A powerful, intimate story of life on the NHS frontline as Dr Saleyha Ahsan films her own journey through four months of the second wave of Covid, fighting to keep patients alive.

videos.title: The Dirty Truth About Your Rubbish
videos.overview: A look at how millions of tonnes of household recycling end up incinerated, hiking carbon emissions, with councils locked into long and expensive waste contracts.

videos.title: The Truth About Long Covid
videos.overview: It is now estimated that as many as 500,000 people have long Covid in the UK. In Bradford, one of our worst hit cities, Dispatches asks can the National Health Service cope with the virus's lasting legacy?

videos.title: The High Street Cash Crisis
videos.overview: Britain's high streets are in turmoil. Antony Barnett digs into the collapse of several chains - from Debenhams to Poundworld - owned by private equity firms. How much are these firms to blame?

videos.title: The Black Maternity Scandal
videos.overview: A C4 documentary detailing the NHS's systemic racism.

videos.title: Low Pay Britain: About Your Job
videos.overview: As Britain emerges from lockdown and Brexit, Dispatches examines the future of work, wages and safety, and the emerging gig economy of brands like Amazon and Deliveroo.

videos.title: Royals for Hire
videos.overview: Antony Barnett goes undercover to see what some of the Queen's family might be prepared to do for cash, including offering access to Kensington Palace and to Vladimir Putin

videos.title: Second Wave: Did the Government Get It Wrong?
videos.overview: Why did two thirds of Britain's Covid deaths come after September 2020? Dispatches examines the role that the Prime Minister's decisions played in the second wave.

videos.title: Football's Gambling Addiction
videos.overview: Ruth Davidson examines the uncomfortable relationship between gambling and football. Why is football so dependent on money from gambling, and what harm might it be causing, particularly to young fans?

videos.title: Undercover in Africa's Secret State
videos.overview: A gripping, eye-opening investigation of Eritrea, one of the world's most secretive regimes, with shocking allegations of torture, detention and forced conscription.

videos.title: Torn Apart: Family Courts Uncovered
videos.overview: An unprecedented look at what's going on behind closed doors in family courts, including shocking personal testimony and footage.

videos.title: India's Rape Scandal
videos.overview: With over 70 Indian politicians facing charges of crimes against women, Ramita Navai investigates two rape cases that have sparked allegations of a cover-up.

videos.title: Cops on Trial
videos.overview: Ellie Flynn reports on the scale of sexual misconduct by serving British police officers, including personal accounts from victims and long term partners of serving officers who have endured domestic violence and abuse.

videos.title: Clapped Out: Is the NHS Broken?
videos.overview: Eighteen months into the worst pandemic in a century, this hard-hitting special travels the country asking some tough questions about the performance of our much-loved NHS.

videos.title: Growing Up Poor: Britain's Hidden Homeless Kids
videos.overview: As lock-down ended and kids went back to school, in Luton, Dispatches examines the devastating impact of overcrowded, unsuitable housing on young lives.

videos.title: How Green Is the Government?
videos.overview: Is Britain really one of the world leaders in fighting against climate change? Dispatches investigates as the COP26 summit is held in Glasgow.

videos.title: Did Brexit Work for Business?
videos.overview: Is Brexit, and the new free trade deal with the EU, the huge success the Government said it would be? Dispatches meets firms struggling with increased costs and dwindling profits.

videos.title: The Truth About Electric Cars
videos.overview: As Britain frets over climate change and fuel shortages, is now a good time to sink tens of thousands of your hard-earned pounds into buying an electric car?

videos.title: Escape from the Taliban
videos.overview: In the immediate aftermath of the Taliban taking Kabul, local journalists film terrified Afghans trying to escape abroad - among them noted female rights activist Zoya Faizi.

videos.title: The Truth About Your Chicken: Dispatches
videos.overview: With over a billion chickens eaten each year in the UK, Dispatches investigates supermarket chicken, animal welfare, and what industrial farming means for our countryside.

videos.title: Vaccine Wars: Truth About Pfizer
videos.overview: Pfizer's Covid vaccine has saved millions of lives around the world. But with rising prices and record profits, is the drug firm profiteering from the pandemic?

videos.title: The Truth About Disability Benefits
videos.overview: An investigation into a series of deaths, including suicide, by disabled benefits claimants. What impact did government failings have on those who died?

videos.title: Boris Johnson: Has He Run Out of Road?
videos.overview: Is Boris Johnson, the great political survivor, finished? Britain's top political interviewer Andrew Neil has the inside track on the Tories in turmoil.

videos.title: China: The Search for the Missing
videos.overview: On the eve of the Winter Olympics, Dispatches investigates allegations of mass surveillance, detention and forced labour in China's north-west.

videos.title: Ukraine: On the Front Line with Johnny Mercer
videos.overview: Former soldier and MP Johnny Mercer meets his Ukrainian political counterparts and heads to the focus of the conflict in Kyiv with explorer Levison Wood.

videos.title: Cadbury Exposed
videos.overview: Undercover in Ghana, Antony Barnett investigates Britain's best-loved chocolate brand and reveals for the first time child labour in its supply chain.

videos.title: Why Are Your Energy Bills So High?
videos.overview: As gas and electricity costs soar, what's the reason for the price hikes? What's the impact on households, and are consumers being properly protected?

videos.title: Are We Losing the War on Terror?
videos.overview: The shocking truth about the Government's de-radicalization programme - a broken system where obvious warning signs of extremism are being missed.

videos.title: Inside the Metaverse: Are You Safe?
videos.overview: Is the next frontier in cyberspace a thrilling alternative world or the new Wild West? Yinka Bokinni goes undercover in virtual reality and is shocked by what she finds.

videos.title: The Enemy Within: The Far Right
videos.overview: A year-long investigation deep undercover reveals the concerning new tactics of Britain's far right - from meddling in by-elections to home schooling.

videos.title: The Truth About Nike and Adidas
videos.overview: With 25 billion pairs of trainers made annually, the industry is the world's 17th largest polluter. Dispatches heads to the Maldives to see what's really going on with our favourite sneakers.

videos.title: MPs Under Threat
videos.overview: Kim Leadbeater MP, investigates threats and abuse faced by MPs. With polarized politics, and social media making it easier to target politicians, is enough being done to protect them?

videos.title: Corrupt Cops: What the Met Knew
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates concerns senior officers were linked to organized crime and that murders went unsolved because of corruption.

videos.title: Ukraine: Life Under Attack
videos.overview: Cate Blanchett narrates the up-close story of the Battle for Kharkiv, told through the eyes of the civilians and emergency workers who bore the brunt of the Russian onslaught.

videos.title: Myanmar: The Forgotten Revolution
videos.overview: A look at the world's forgotten civil war, where over 20,000 people have been reported dead, and thousands are fighting against a military coup that has removed elected government.

videos.title: Airport Chaos Undercover
videos.overview: With the summer holidays in full swing, reporter Jane Moore goes undercover in one of Britain's busiest airports, with the truth about delays, cancellations and baggage chaos.

videos.title: Why Is My Car So Expensive?
videos.overview: What's the real story behind the soaring cost of new and second-hand cars? As the car industry pulls in huge profits, Dispatches has top tips on how not to get ripped off.

videos.title: Britain's Water Scandal
videos.overview: Jimmy Doherty investigates Britain's water companies dumping untreated sewage into our rivers and seas. Why have companies been getting away with it for so long?

videos.title: Broke: Britain's Debt Emergency
videos.overview: With Britain in the worst cost of living crisis in decades, Dispatches follows Citizens Advice Bureau debt advisors and three stories of extreme hardship and poverty.

videos.title: Britain's Evicted Kids
videos.overview: Dispatches lifts the lid on the reality of life for thousands of families across the country at risk of eviction, and how losing a home impacts the youngest members of our society.

videos.title: Hospital Undercover Are They Safe?
videos.overview: On World Mental Health Day, a year-long investigation reveals that an NHS trust responsible for serious failures resulting in multiple deaths, still isn't keeping patients safe.

videos.title: Trapped, Disabled & Abused
videos.overview: Disabled people are twice as likely to experience domestic abuse than non-disabled people. Dispatches reveals a shocking lack of awareness and support for survivors.

videos.title: Cops in Crisis
videos.overview: Is British policing fit for purpose? Dispatches reports on forces in special measures, talk of a toxic culture, funding cuts, and crimes receiving little or no investigation.

videos.title: Strippers, Spies & Russian Money
videos.overview: The extraordinary story of Russia's covert efforts to corrupt British democracy and politics in the years before invading Ukraine. MI5 declined to comment on the programme for operational reasons.

videos.title: Undercover Ambulance: NHS Chaos
videos.overview: Secret footage filmed over the winter reveals ambulance workers battling the odds and A&E departments overwhelmed as patients suffer needless harm and death.

videos.title: Locked Away: Our Autism Scandal
videos.overview: Autistic patients trapped in mental health units tell their stories, revealing a system of poor treatment, abuse and long stretches inside with their symptoms only getting worse.

videos.title: Britain's Forgotten Pensioners
videos.overview: More than two million pensioners are living in poverty in the UK. Dispatches follows four older people through the winter as they struggle to make ends meet.

videos.title: Boris, the Lord & the Russian Spy
videos.overview: The full story of Boris Johnson's friendship with press baron Evgeny Lebedev and his dad Alexander, an ex-KGB spy, revealing the secret fears of security services

videos.title: Sri Lanka's Easter Bombings
videos.overview: A Dispatches special reveals shocking new evidence on Sri Lanka's deadly Easter bombings of 2019. High-placed whistle blowers allege top-level complicity by officials inside the Sri Lankan government.

videos.title: Russell Brand: In Plain Sight
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates Russell Brand's treatment of women. The British comedian, television personality and radio talker Russell Brand is accused of abusing women close to him for several years. An investigation by Channel4.

videos.title: Hunting Russia's Lost Boys
videos.overview: The intimate, emotional story of the Russian women taking huge risks fighting for the truth about their sons, husbands and brothers missing in Ukraine.

videos.title: Hunt for Ukraine's Stolen Children
videos.overview: Along the dangerous borderlands of war-torn Ukraine, Dispatches follows investigators searching for evidence of the abduction and deportation of thousands of Ukrainian kids.

videos.title: Secrets & Power: China in the UK
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates Chinese state interference with UK institutions and repression of dissidents on UK soil. Undercover filming reveals a suspected Chinese spy engaging with a UK-based activist.

videos.title: How Safe Is Your Turkey?
videos.overview: In the run-up to Christmas, nine million turkeys will be sold across Britain. Dispatches investigates food safety concerns at one producer.

videos.title: Less for More: The Truth About Food Prices
videos.overview: Harry Wallop investigates Britain's soaring food prices, and how some supermarkets have reacted to protect profits. He discovers how some products have secretly been reformulated, with cheaper ingredients replacing more expensive items.

videos.title: Coca-Cola's Dirty Secret
videos.overview: What's the environmental impact of the UK's huge soft drink habit? With a thirsty nation getting through two billion plastic bottles a year, and the same for cans, do Coke's recycling claims stand up?

videos.title: The War on Britain's Motorists
videos.overview: Potholes everywhere. Controversial Low Traffic Neighbourhoods and electric vehicle confusion too. Car journalist Ginny Buckley asks is this the worst time ever to be a motorist in the UK?

videos.title: Kill Zone: Inside Gaza
videos.overview: The story of the Israeli military assault on Gaza. Seen through the eyes of children, journalists and doctors, Dispatches takes an unflinching look at the horrific challenges and heartbreaking loss.

videos.title: The Truth About Temu
videos.overview: What's the story behind the runaway success of the addictive Chinese shopping app? With half a billion downloads worldwide, are some of Temu's rock-bottom prices and products too good to be true?

videos.title: Rubbish Tip Britain
videos.overview: A look inside the lucrative world of waste crime with video, surveillance footage and interviews from insiders. Exposing how banned waste has been dumped for years in a major landfill site, seemingly unnoticed by the authorities, while posing a risk to human health. This documentary reveals new satellite data suggesting hundreds of unregulated waste dumps are being operated in plain sight and investigates evidence of the growing role of organisations engaging in illegal fly-tipping, with little fear of action against them.

videos.title: Undercover A&E: NHS in Crisis
videos.overview: Undercover report filmed over two months at an NHS Accident and Emergency Department, which exposes the suffering and dangers patients face on a daily basis. The programme features footage of seriously ill patients forced to sleep on chairs for up to two days because there are no beds, and a dangerous superbug outbreak linked to overcrowding and falling hygiene standards.

videos.title: Can AI Steal Your Vote?
videos.overview: Election campaigners and experts have warned that artificial intelligence tools could risk politically motivated disinformation flooding social media feeds in ways that recently seemed unimaginable. The fear is that deepfakes and other AI-generated material could influence votes. Cathy Newman reports on the issue, illustrating the effect that AI could have on 12 households of undecided voters. The homes are fed AI-generated material advised by political experts, with the residents none the wiser. Will the experiment succeed? If so, what does it say about the power of AI to influence the vote?

videos.title: Britain's Unsolved Crimewave
videos.overview: Analysing police data, Dispatches reveals local hotspots where 100% of neighbourhood crimes go unsolved. The team watch a theft in action and go on the trail of the criminals.

videos.title: Barbie's Dirty Secrets
videos.overview: With Barbiemania putting toy maker Mattel back in the limelight, Dispatches goes undercover in one of Mattel's factories, exposing the reality for workers making the famous dolls

videos.title: Vinted's Dirty Laundry
videos.overview: The online secondhand clothes app Vinted is booming. Is its soar-away success too good to be true? Dispatches uncovers the truth behind some of the products sold on the platform.

videos.title: The King, The Prince & Their Secret Millions
videos.overview: For years, the royals kept details of some of their wealth secret. Dispatches reveals what they have kept under wraps - about who is paying them, and for what.

videos.title: Britain's Shoplifting Gangs Exposed
videos.overview: In this high-stakes true crime investigation, Dispatches goes undercover to expose the organised criminal networks behind the UK's shoplifting epidemic.

videos.title: Britain's Benefits Scandal
videos.overview: With the recent rise in working-age people on sickness benefits - many of them under 35 - Dispatches asks what's driving the surge?

videos.title: Skinny Jab Scandal
videos.overview: Undercover reporting reveals major flaws in how skinny jabs are sold at Boots and finds registered NHS nurses prescribing jabs to patients who aren't overweight.

videos.title: Delivered to a Predator: Al Fayed's Fixer
videos.overview: Reporter Cathy Newman investigates and tracks down the woman who facilitated Mohamed Al Fayed's rape and sexual abuse of women at Harrods for over a decade.

videos.title: Undercover: The Great Tagging Scandal
videos.overview: As the government release thousands to ease prison numbers, Dispatches is undercover inside the company paid millions to monitor offenders and keep us all safe.

videos.title: Britain's Car Theft Gangs Exposed
videos.overview: Every eight minutes a car is stolen in Britain. Dispatches goes undercover on the tail of the thieves driving this car-crime epidemic.

videos.title: Will Nigel Farage Be Prime Minister?
videos.overview: With Reform UK topping polls and running councils, are we on the verge of a political earthquake? And do Reform UK have what it takes to govern?

videos.title: Trump: Moscow's Man in the White House?
videos.overview: What's the truth about Trump's relationship with Putin? Insiders share a unique behind-the-scenes view on the greatest political story of the decade.

videos.title: 999 Undercover: NHS in Crisis
videos.overview: A Dispatches reporter goes undercover inside a 999 control room to reveal the truth about our overstretched ambulance services.

videos.title: Will AI Take My Job?
videos.overview: Will AI leave millions of Britain's skilled work force without a job? From health care to the law and more, Dispatches investigates, pitting human versus machine to find out who's the best worker.

videos.title: The Prince vs. The Paper: Harry, Hacking & The Mail
videos.overview: As a trial date approaches, the latest on Prince Harry's case against the Daily Mail and Mail on Sunday - who Harry accuses of phone hacking and bugging.

videos.title: Hunting Britain's Parcel Thieves
videos.overview: Every seven seconds a parcel is stolen in Britain. With Christmas just around the corner, Dispatches is on a mission to catch the crooks behind the escalating doormat deliveries crime wave.

videos.title: Palestine Action: The Truth Behind the Ban
videos.overview: Dispatches investigates why the government banned direct action group Palestine Action, a decision that has sparked intense debate and led to thousands of arrests.

videos.title: Keir Starmer: Where Did It All Go Wrong?
videos.overview: Lewis Goodall looks back at a torrid first two years as prime minister for Sir Keir Starmer, and asks how he went from winning a 174-seat majority to becoming the most unpopular PM since records began.

videos.title: Click to Kill: The AI War Machine
videos.overview: With unique access in Ukraine, in Israel and with the US army, this documentary charts the new technological arms race, from AI to drones. Will warfare become less destructive or even more brutal?

videos.title: Hunting Britain's Fugitives
videos.overview: Thousands of criminals, many of whom are accused of serious, violent crimes, are currently on the run in a hidden criminal justice crisis. From UK safe-houses to Thailand, Matt Shea is on their trail.
